items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review paper examines exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by carrying bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids, with a focus on understanding their molecular regulation and clinical utility. The authors synthesize current knowledge of the molecular machinery governing exosome biogenesis and cargo loading, including the roles of endosomal sorting complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications that collectively determine cargo heterogeneity. The review also surveys modern analytical technologies and omics platforms used to characterize exosomal content for diagnostic applications, particularly in liquid biopsies for cancer, metabolic disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases. On the therapeutic side, the paper explores the potential of both native and engineered exosomes for drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, and discusses ongoing clinical translation efforts. The authors identify persistent translational barriers such as isolation standardization and targeting specificity, while highlighting emerging approaches including synthetic exosome mimetics and artificial intelligence-driven diagnostics as strategies to advance exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired illness with high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature synthesis covering the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside an evaluation of both conventional and emerging diagnostic technologies. The review critically assesses current antifungal therapeutic strategies, including empiric and targeted regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing problem of antifungal resistance, with particular attention to the potential role of combination therapy. Novel agents currently in clinical trials and compounds directed at new fungal targets are highlighted as part of the evolving treatment landscape. Looking ahead, the authors identify artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches as promising future directions for improving candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Efficient Event Generation for High-Multiplicity LHC Processes: An End-to-End GPU Workflow with Normalizing Flows
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of generating large samples of unweighted events for high-multiplicity particle collision processes at the LHC, where standard approaches are bottlenecked by costly matrix-element evaluations and poor unweighting efficiencies. The authors developed the first fully GPU-resident end-to-end event-generation workflow, combining normalizing flow models as phase-space proposals with the parton-level generator Pepper, keeping all data exchange between the control layer and the matrix-element evaluator directly in device memory to minimize overhead. The normalizing flows are trained using online updates with sample replay and deployed across multiple partonic subprocesses, with the study comparing subprocess-specific flows against grouped conditional flows that share parameters among related subprocesses. The workflow was benchmarked on several high-multiplicity processes including multi-jet and top-quark pair production, demonstrating end-to-end speedups of up to two orders of magnitude over standalone Pepper on four high-end GPUs, reducing what would otherwise be a multi-week computation to less than a single day. The authors conclude that this approach makes billion-event production practical and offers a viable path toward relieving the Monte Carlo statistics bottleneck in high-multiplicity collider physics analyses.
items.citation: Enrico Bothmann, Joshua Isaacson, Claudius Krause et al.. Efficient Event Generation for High-Multiplicity LHC Processes: An End-to-End GPU Workflow with Normalizing Flows. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Maxwell's Demon in Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Cooling Information Flow and Entropy Balance
items.summary: This paper examines Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms through the lens of thermodynamic analogies, specifically by drawing a formal parallel between the accept/reject mechanism and Maxwell's Demon. The authors identify the acceptance module as the demon, which measures proposed moves, stores outcomes in a single decision bit, and uses that information to guide probability currents toward the target distribution. They show that the decision bit carries genuine Shannon mutual information about the proposal, but only its directional component contributes to what the authors term a cooling information flow. The central result is a decomposition of the relative-entropy relaxation rate into two distinct contributions: a useful cooling term and a housekeeping circulation term arising from nonreversibility. This framework provides a principled way to separate productive convergence toward the target distribution from irreducible entropy production associated with nonequilibrium steady-state circulation in non-reversible chains.
items.citation: Masayuki Ohzeki. Maxwell's Demon in Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Cooling Information Flow and Entropy Balance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dirac Surface States and Nonlocal Quantum Tunneling in Topological Semiconductor Mo$_2$SeTe$_3$ for High-Performance Tunnel FETs
items.summary: This study investigates the quasi-two-dimensional transition-metal chalcogenide Mo₂SeTe₃ as a candidate material for low-power quantum electronic devices using first-principles calculations combined with device-level simulations. The material is identified as a weak topological semiconductor, exhibiting spin-orbit coupling-driven band inversion, an indirect bulk bandgap, and symmetry-protected Dirac surface states confirmed through Wannier charge-center evolution and Z₂ invariant analysis with weak topological indices. Beyond its topological properties, Mo₂SeTe₃ demonstrates dynamical and mechanical stability, strong optical anisotropy, broad infrared-to-visible absorption, and favorable thermoelectric transport characteristics including enhanced carrier mobility under n-type doping. A dual-source tunnel field-effect transistor implemented via TCAD simulations with nonlocal band-to-band tunneling achieves subthreshold switching below the thermionic limit, a high ON/OFF current ratio, and improved tunneling efficiency attributed to SOC-induced orbital hybridization and topologically enhanced interband coupling. The authors conclude that Mo₂SeTe₃ represents a multifunctional quantum material platform suitable for both topological applications and next-generation energy-efficient nanoelectronics.
items.citation: Zafar Sadik Mehrub, Suvodip Kundu Arnob, Md. Tareq Mahmud et al.. Dirac Surface States and Nonlocal Quantum Tunneling in Topological Semiconductor Mo$_2$SeTe$_3$ for High-Performance Tunnel FETs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dynamics of localized solutions in three core coupled waveguides with quasi-periodic nonlinearity
items.summary: The paper investigates how solitons behave in a system of three coupled waveguides where the nonlinearity governing inter-waveguide interactions is spatially modulated in a quasi-periodic fashion. By varying the modulation parameters, the authors analyze the evolution of soliton profiles and their mutual interactions within this coupled system. They find that the interplay between quasi-periodic nonlinearity and waveguide parameters gives rise to complex dynamics, including regimes of soliton attraction and repulsion. The results advance understanding of how quasi-periodic nonlinear modulation shapes localized wave behavior in multi-core waveguide systems, with suggested relevance for nonlinear optics and photonic device applications.
items.citation: Bruno M. Miranda, Ardiley T. Avelar, Wesley B. Cardoso et al.. Dynamics of localized solutions in three core coupled waveguides with quasi-periodic nonlinearity. arXiv. 2026

The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, emphasizing how innovations in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have substantially improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transforms conventional sensors into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically addresses persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation approaches such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic sample pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors outline a vision for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-integrated data management, and standardized validation pipelines to facilitate the deployment of robust, regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a versatile and sustainable platform for addressing challenges across energy, environmental, and healthcare domains. The authors survey the synthesis chemistry and property modification strategies that underpin graphene oxide's distinctive characteristics, including its tunable band gap, high surface area, structural flexibility, and capacity for surface functionalization spanning zero- to three-dimensional architectures. The review covers a broad range of applications, including adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and microplastics, photocatalytic hydrogen production and carbon dioxide reduction, battery technologies, ultra-sensitive molecular detection via surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and biomedical uses. The authors highlight that graphene oxide can perform effectively as a standalone material across these diverse fields, underscoring its multifunctional and transformative potential. However, the review also acknowledges persistent challenges such as scalability limitations, long-term stability concerns, and reproducibility issues, and proposes potential solutions to support sustainable and industrially viable future applications.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review paper examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infections with high mortality and substantial healthcare burden. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside a critical evaluation of existing diagnostic methods and their limitations. The review assesses emerging diagnostic technologies with potential to improve detection performance, and thoroughly examines therapeutic strategies including empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing challenge of antifungal resistance. The paper also highlights advances in drug development, including agents in clinical trials and compounds targeting novel fungal pathways. Looking forward, the authors explore future directions such as artificial intelligence applications in diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and combination treatment strategies, aiming to guide clinicians and researchers in addressing evolving challenges in candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.
items.summary: This paper developed a dual-function electrochemical biosensor capable of both detecting and destroying bacterial pathogens using a single electrode material. The researchers synthesized silver nanoparticle-decorated metal-covalent organic framework composites that formed a nanoflower-like structure, then functionalized the resulting electrode with aptamers specific to Staphylococcus aureus. The biosensor achieved highly sensitive detection of the target bacterium across a broad concentration range with a limit of detection of a single colony-forming unit per milliliter. Beyond detection, the material's photocatalytic activity enabled near-complete inactivation of captured bacteria through reactive oxygen species generation under visible light within minutes, after which the electrode could be regenerated and reused. The work demonstrates that metal-covalent organic framework composites can serve as a unified platform for simultaneous pathogen sensing and antibacterial action, with implications for infectious disease surveillance and control.
items.citation: Bai Y, Xiao L, Cai L et al.. Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: A Modular APEX Biosensor Enables Sensitive and Visualized Monitoring of Viral Protease Activity.
items.summary: The paper developed modular biosensors designed to detect viral protease activity within living cells and to screen antiviral drug candidates under physiologically relevant conditions. Traditional approaches such as fluorescent protein assays and FRET-based methods suffer from non-specific conformational interference and fail to accurately capture intracellular inhibitory effects, motivating the need for a new platform. The researchers engineered two biosensors based on split ascorbate peroxidase fragments that reassemble upon protease-mediated cleavage of a specific recognition sequence, restoring enzymatic activity and generating amplified fluorescent signals. Using the coronavirus main protease as a model, one sensor achieved an exceptionally high signal-to-noise ratio for enzymatic detection, while the other accurately identified potent inhibitors and avoided the false positives common to conventional methods. By simply swapping the protease recognition sequence, the platform can be adapted to monitor proteases from a range of viruses, offering a flexible and reliable intracellular tool to accelerate broad-spectrum antiviral drug discovery.
items.citation: Li B, Dong B, Chen Y et al.. A Modular APEX Biosensor Enables Sensitive and Visualized Monitoring of Viral Protease Activity.. Virologica Sinica. 2026

items.title: Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Escherichia coli* in neonatal sepsis, where conventional blood culture is slow and often insufficiently sensitive. Researchers developed a multiple cross-displacement amplification assay paired with a lateral flow biosensor targeting the *uidA* gene, using a ten-primer design optimized to run at a single temperature for forty minutes. The assay achieved femtogram-level sensitivity with no cross-reactivity against non-*E. coli* strains, and the complete workflow from nucleic acid extraction to visual result was completed within approximately one hour. Clinical validation using blood and cerebrospinal fluid specimens from neonates with suspected *E. coli* infection showed the assay achieved complete concordance with quantitative PCR while detecting a substantially higher proportion of positive cases than conventional culture. The authors conclude that this method offers a rapid, sensitive, and operationally simple approach well suited to point-of-care and resource-limited settings for early diagnosis of neonatal *E. coli* infection.
items.citation: Xiao R, Zou P, Zhou J et al.. Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.
items.summary: This study developed a biosensor for detecting *Salmonella typhimurium*, a major cause of foodborne illness, at extremely low concentrations. The system integrates DNAzyme-catalysed amplification with hybridization chain reaction to convert pathogen-specific signals into branched DNA nanowires bearing protospacer adjacent motif sequences, which then activate CRISPR/Cas12a to cleave the nanowires and restore a quenched fluorescent signal. This cascade of target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment steps enables ultrasensitive detection across a broad linear range, achieving a very low limit of detection. The biosensor operates rapidly, requires straightforward handling, and demonstrated high sensitivity and selectivity under optimized conditions. The authors also propose that the platform is adaptable to other foodborne pathogens by substituting the recognition and primer sequences, suggesting broad applicability in food safety monitoring.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Liu Y, Yue X, Li B et al.. Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid, accurate detection of *Escherichia coli* O157:H7, a significant foodborne pathogen, by developing a one-pot CRISPR/Cas13-based biosensor capable of simultaneously targeting two key genetic markers that define the pathogen's serotype. The system exploited the distinct collateral cleavage preferences of two different Cas13 proteins to create dual fluorescence channels, allowing serotype-specific identification while reducing false positives, and integrated gene amplification via recombinase polymerase amplification, transcription, and CRISPR-mediated sensing into a single reaction tube. The biosensor achieved high sensitivity at a low detection limit and was validated using a mouse infection model, with results from fecal samples consistent with standard PCR methods. Compared to conventional CRISPR diagnostics, this dual-channel approach improves specificity and serotype discrimination while remaining simple, rapid, and suitable for field deployment, offering potential utility in clinical diagnostics, food safety monitoring, and infectious disease surveillance.
items.citation: He Y, Lin X, Zhang X et al.. Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.. JACS Au. 2026

items.title: Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor designed for rapid, point-of-care detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and emerging pathogen targets. The platform uses disposable graphene foam electrodes functionalized with pyrene-modified peptide nucleic acid probes, which are attached via π-π stacking to preserve the material's electronic properties and high surface area, enabling amplification-free and label-free nucleic acid detection. A key innovation is a heat-assisted functionalization protocol that reduces preparation time from hours to minutes while maintaining sensor performance. The biosensor demonstrated sensitive and selective detection of the colistin resistance gene, discriminating the true target from non-complementary sequences, and was readily retargeted to a second resistance gene simply by swapping the probe. The authors conclude that the platform offers a reproducible, scalable approach to decentralized molecular diagnostics for antimicrobial resistance and pandemic preparedness.
items.citation: Wang KY, Schulze H, Lozano Sanchez P et al.. Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current state and translational obstacles of extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics, which have gained attention for their biocompatibility, ability to carry biomolecules, and capacity to cross biological barriers. The authors systematically catalogue the core impediments preventing most EV products from advancing beyond preclinical stages, including difficulties in isolation, storage stability, characterization, biosafety evaluation, and quality control. They then survey emerging technologies proposed to address these bottlenecks, such as advanced bioreactors for scalable production, microfluidic platforms for high-purity separation, single-vesicle analysis to manage heterogeneity, and machine learning tools to support standardization and clinical decision-making. The review concludes by outlining future priorities around standardizing production processes, improving safety assessment frameworks, and achieving regulatory compliance. Overall, the authors argue that resolving these intertwined technical and regulatory challenges is essential to accelerating the translation of EV therapies into clinical practice.
items.citation: Jing Zhang, Yuanwei Pan, Peng She et al.. From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics. Theranostics. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review examines the dual role of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they serve both as essential signaling molecules at physiological levels and as drivers of cellular damage when produced in excess. The paper synthesizes current knowledge on the major types, cellular sources, and molecular mechanisms by which ROS regulate normal physiology and contribute to oxidative stress-related pathology. The authors survey contemporary and emerging methodologies for detecting and quantifying ROS in clinical and preclinical settings, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging approaches. The review connects oxidative stress mechanisms to the pathophysiology of major diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular conditions, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders. The authors conclude by advocating for precision redox medicine strategies that integrate improved ROS detection technologies with targeted antioxidant-based diagnostics and therapeutics.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: A review of applications of machine learning in quantum dots research
items.summary: This review examines how machine learning has been applied across the breadth of quantum dot research, spanning experimental device control, materials synthesis, sensing, photonic applications, and computational modeling of quantum systems. The authors surveyed recent data-driven approaches with particular attention to how these methods are embedded within established physical workflows rather than deployed independently. They found that machine learning most commonly serves to replace time-consuming fitting procedures, guide experimental sampling, or approximate computationally intensive simulations, with recurring methodological patterns including supervised learning on limited datasets, transfer learning across device instances, and hybrid approaches that incorporate physical constraints. The review also identifies persistent limitations such as dataset bias, poor cross-laboratory transferability, absence of standardized benchmarks, and inadequate treatment of uncertainty. The authors conclude that machine learning is best understood as a complementary tool whose reliability depends critically on integration with physical insight, sound experimental design, and rigorous validation.
items.citation: Ivan Malashin, Dmitry Martysyuk, Vladimir Nelyub et al.. A review of applications of machine learning in quantum dots research. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: Classical versus non-classical photon states for detecting vacuum non-linearity
items.summary: The paper investigates whether the detectability of quantum electrodynamic vacuum nonlinearity can be enhanced by modifying the initial quantum state of light used in experimental schemes designed to verify this fundamental prediction. Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum itself behaves as a nonlinear optical medium, and many verification schemes look for photons appearing in modes that would otherwise be empty. The authors consider replacing the vacuum state in those signal modes with either classical or non-classical photon states, such as squeezed light, and analyze the resulting effect on measurement sensitivity. They find that injecting such modified photon states into the relevant modes can significantly improve the detectability of the vacuum nonlinearity signal compared to standard approaches.
items.citation: N. Ahmadiniaz, C. Kohlfürst, R. Shaisultanov et al.. Classical versus non-classical photon states for detecting vacuum non-linearity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Mining beyond Earth with Space Robots: Exploration, Sampling, and Extraction
items.summary: This paper provides a comprehensive review of space mining robotics, covering the technologies and systems needed to extract resources such as helium-3, water, minerals, and asteroid deposits for sustained human space exploration and commercial purposes. The authors propose a systematic six-stage architecture that organizes space mining activities into three broad phases: exploration via remote sensing and in situ robotic detection, sampling through single- and multi-robot excavation, and extraction culminating in resource integration for in situ construction or transport back to Earth. The review also catalogs available research resources including real-world mission data, terrestrial analog datasets, and simulation environments to support the field. The paper identifies key open challenges posed by harsh space environments, communication delays, and high launch costs, and outlines a strategic research roadmap aimed at advancing autonomous robotic systems to close existing technological gaps. Ultimately, the authors frame these developments as essential steps toward establishing a sustainable off-world economy.
items.citation: Dong Li, Dujun Nie, Xiaotong Zhang et al.. Mining beyond Earth with Space Robots: Exploration, Sampling, and Extraction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: This paper examines the ethical and governance challenges that arise when autonomous AI diagnostic agents are deployed in sub-Saharan African healthcare settings, where patients often remain unaware that non-human systems are making or influencing clinical decisions about them. The authors argue that existing frameworks for AI accountability and transparency in healthcare are predominantly clinician-centered and assume robust regulatory environments that do not reflect the realities of low-resource contexts, leaving a structural accountability gap from a patient perspective. Drawing on documented cases of AI deployment in Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana, the paper demonstrates that problems around inadequate informed consent, limited human oversight, and poorly adapted explainability are already manifesting in active systems. In response, the authors synthesize literature on informed consent, algorithmic accountability, and explainable AI to propose three foundational principles: agent-aware informed consent, mandatory human override mechanisms, and contextually adapted explainability. These principles are presented as a practical minimum standard intended to guide developers, health system administrators, and policymakers in regions where formal AI regulation has yet to mature.
items.citation: Percy Brown, Kweku Yamoah. Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) in a timely manner, noting that conventional machine learning approaches relying on clinical and laboratory data introduce problematic delays. To overcome this, the authors developed a Time-Aware transformer-based model that operates exclusively on respiratory data collected from home ventilators, enabling a low-latency monitoring scenario. The model generates patient representations that capture both symptom patterns and their temporal progression within the ventilator data stream. Experimental results showed that this approach outperformed traditional methods across multiple classification tasks, suggesting it could meaningfully improve the speed and accuracy of AECOPD prediction in real-world home settings.
items.citation: Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Dongyang Wang et al.. Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD. arXiv. 2026

items.title: VLASS Discovery of a Luminous Galactic Radio Transient Evolving on Decade Timescales
items.summary: This paper presents a detailed multiwavelength study of a newly discovered Galactic radio transient, VT J1906+0849, identified in the Very Large Array Sky Survey after more than two decades of non-detection in prior surveys. Radio observations trace the source's evolution from its first detection in 2005 through a peak flux and subsequent decline, with a late rebrightening, while its low Galactic latitude and optical-infrared counterpart confirm a Galactic origin at a distance placing it among the most radio-luminous known Galactic transients. Despite spectral signatures consistent with synchrotron self-absorption, interferometric observations reveal that the radio-emitting region has undergone little to no expansion over several years, and the source is unexpectedly faint in X-rays compared to known X-ray binaries. Near-infrared spectroscopy identifies a broad emission line interpreted as blueshifted hydrogen recombination emission tracing a persistent, asymmetric outflow of roughly two thousand kilometers per second. The authors propose that VT J1906+0849 may represent a young analog of the microquasar SS 433, in which a dense disk wind confines a continuously powered synchrotron jet, simultaneously explaining the compact radio structure and the suppression of bright X-ray emission.
items.citation: Jessie M. Miller, Gregg Hallinan, Dillon Dong et al.. VLASS Discovery of a Luminous Galactic Radio Transient Evolving on Decade Timescales. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Requirements Engineering: Evidence of the Negative Effect of LLMs on Requirements Inspection
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language model assistance improves human performance on requirements inspection, a software engineering practice aimed at identifying defects in requirements documents early in development. Using a controlled crossover experiment, participants inspected textual specifications both with and without LLM support, identifying and classifying requirements smells by type and severity while their task duration was recorded, with Bayesian regression models used to analyze outcomes. Contrary to optimistic expectations, LLM support was found to negatively affect smell detection accuracy while having no meaningful impact on severity classification or inspection time. The study also identified a learning effect across experimental periods, whereby skill development was attenuated when participants began the task with LLM assistance rather than without it. These findings suggest that LLM support not only fails to enhance novice inspectors' performance but may also impede the natural acquisition of requirements inspection skills when introduced from the outset.
items.citation: Giovanna Broccia, Julian Frattini, Chetan Arora et al.. Human-AI Collaboration in Requirements Engineering: Evidence of the Negative Effect of LLMs on Requirements Inspection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.
items.summary: This study examined the real-world diagnostic performance and economic implications of syndromic multiplex-PCR panel testing for acute infections across four clinical syndromes at a southern Italian hospital over nearly two years. Researchers retrospectively analysed thousands of distinct diagnostic episodes using panels targeting central nervous system, upper respiratory, lower respiratory, and gastrointestinal pathogens, tracking positivity rates, pathogen distribution, and resistance marker profiles. The most striking finding was that nearly three-fifths of all determinations yielded entirely negative results, with a pronounced gradient across panel types: the meningitis/encephalitis panel was negative in nine out of ten cases, while the pneumonia panel had the lowest negativity rate. Pathogen ecology varied meaningfully by syndrome, with viral agents dominating central nervous system infections, rhinovirus/enterovirus leading respiratory findings, and diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes and Clostridioides difficile driving gastrointestinal positives, while resistance markers clustered in polymicrobial Enterobacterales infections. Based on these findings, the authors advocate for targeted stewardship interventions including cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis gating, tiered respiratory testing algorithms, restriction of gastrointestinal panels to community-onset diarrhoea, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A specimens to close a identified surveillance gap for novel or zoonotic strains.
items.citation: Chirizzi D, Spedicato A, Bianco G et al.. Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: 320 Diagnostic stewardship of a multiplex pneumonia PCR panel leads to cost savings and more appropriate patient care
items.citation: Ronne R, Kracker A, Salgado C. 320 Diagnostic stewardship of a multiplex pneumonia PCR panel leads to cost savings and more appropriate patient care. Antimicrobial stewardship & healthcare epidemiology : ASHE. 2026

items.title: Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.
items.summary: This study examined how the lifting of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions affected the detection patterns of respiratory pathogens in children presenting with fever or respiratory symptoms at a pediatric center in Guangzhou, subtropical southern China. Researchers retrospectively analyzed nasopharyngeal swab samples from children under sixteen years old, using a consistent twelve-pathogen multiplex PCR platform across both a pre-lifting and a post-lifting period, with a season-matched comparison focused on the same months across two years to minimize seasonal bias. Following the lifting of restrictions, the season-matched analysis revealed notably higher detection rates of Influenza A, respiratory syncytial virus, and human rhinovirus, while Influenza B and human metapneumovirus declined substantially. The post-lifting cohort also included a higher proportion of infants and greater rates of lower respiratory tract diagnoses, though the authors caution that changes in healthcare-seeking behavior and admission thresholds may confound clinical comparisons. The findings highlight the value of continued multiplex surveillance and age-targeted prevention strategies, while emphasizing that causal attribution to the lifting of restrictions remains uncertain given residual confounding by seasonality and concurrent SARS-CoV-2 circulation.
items.citation: Hua L, Liang W, Li W et al.. Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Scenario-Driven Rapid Testing for Top Pathogens in Pediatric Respiratory Infections: Clinical and Economic Value from Emergency Triage to Precision Anti-Infective Management in the PICU.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how rapid diagnostic testing for pediatric respiratory infections can be optimized to deliver clinical and economic value across diverse healthcare settings. The authors address the fundamental diagnostic challenge that viral, bacterial, and atypical pathogens produce overlapping clinical presentations in children, driving inappropriate empirical antimicrobial use. Rather than evaluating diagnostic technologies in isolation, they organize existing evidence around a scenario-driven framework in which "top pathogens" are defined contextually by factors such as age group, syndrome, season, care setting, transmissibility, and antimicrobial resistance relevance. The review argues that rapid pathogen detection alone does not reliably reduce antibiotic prescribing or costs unless testing is applied to the right patient within a predefined clinical decision pathway, spanning emergency triage through PICU and outbreak settings. The authors ultimately propose implementation principles integrating diagnostic stewardship, antimicrobial stewardship, and local epidemiology as a practical bridge between broad syndromic panels and precision infectious disease management in children.
items.citation: Chen J, Wang H, Li Y et al.. Scenario-Driven Rapid Testing for Top Pathogens in Pediatric Respiratory Infections: Clinical and Economic Value from Emergency Triage to Precision Anti-Infective Management in the PICU.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).
items.summary: This study investigated the causes of severe acute respiratory infections among hospitalized adults in northern Thailand during the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. Researchers retrospectively analyzed respiratory samples from adults admitted with SARI symptoms at a regional hospital in Chiang Mai, testing specimens using multiplex real-time PCR capable of detecting a broad range of respiratory viruses and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Nearly half of patients tested positive for at least one pathogen, with adenovirus and rhinovirus being the most commonly detected agents, and co-infections occurring in a notable proportion of cases. Seasonal patterns emerged, with influenza A and rhinovirus peaking in January while adenovirus and enterovirus circulated throughout the study period. The authors conclude that enhanced rapid molecular diagnostics and pathogen-specific surveillance are needed to reduce empiric antibiotic overuse and improve clinical management in the post-pandemic era.
items.citation: Kham-Kjing N, Kawila R, Tariyo P et al.. Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.
items.summary: This study addressed the diagnostic challenge of bovine respiratory disease, a complex multi-pathogen syndrome, by developing and validating the first multiplex quantitative PCR platform for simultaneous detection of ten viral and bacterial BRD pathogens in Brazil. The researchers standardized the system across multiple assay configurations and evaluated its performance using standard curve analysis, repeatability, and reproducibility testing, then applied it to nasal swab samples from dairy cattle in southern Brazil. The platform demonstrated robust analytical performance across all targeted pathogens, with high sensitivity, efficiency, and consistency between singleplex and multiplex formats. Field application revealed that the majority of sampled cattle were positive for at least one pathogen, with bacterial agents predominating and co-infections occurring across multiple combinations, while pathogen detection patterns were significantly influenced by animal age, season, and farm-level factors. The authors conclude that this validated multiplex system will enable cost-effective, rapid simultaneous pathogen detection and advance understanding of BRD epidemiology and pathogenesis in Brazil.
items.citation: Rodriguez MC, Silva IV, Perotta JH et al.. Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations
items.summary: This paper examines the genus *Enterococcus*, which comprises commensal bacteria found in the gastrointestinal tracts of humans and animals, various environments, and diverse food sources. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of the probiotic potential, antimicrobial applications, and safety profiles of beneficial enterococcal strains. These bacteria are increasingly used as protective cultures, antibiotic alternatives, and probiotics, with roles in pathogen control, microbiome modulation, food fermentation, and the production of bioactive compounds such as bacteriocins. However, their association with healthcare-associated infections and the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance genes raises significant safety concerns that necessitate rigorous evaluation before deployment. The review aims to serve as a broad reference resource for researchers, regulators, and practitioners working in agrifood systems and healthcare contexts.
items.citation: Ojonugwa Precious John, Kayode Olayinka Afolabi, Anayochukwu Chibuike Ngene et al.. Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America
items.summary: This study investigated the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b into Antarctica, where it poses a serious threat to polar wildlife. Researchers detected the virus in carcasses of eight species across the South Shetland Islands during two consecutive austral summers, then performed whole-genome sequencing, mutational profiling, and phylogenetic reconstruction to trace the origins and transmission history of these viruses. The analysis revealed that the detected strains were not derived from a single introduction but instead descended from multiple independent introduction events. One group of strains clustered with H5N1 previously found in marine mammals in South America, consistent with at least two separate introductions into Antarctica, while a second group clustered with strains from South Georgia, linking to both regional seabirds and a previously documented Antarctic detection. The findings demonstrate substantial epidemiological connectivity between South America and Antarctica, with South Georgia acting as an intermediary stepping stone facilitating virus spread into the polar region.
items.citation: Maria Ogrzewalska, Ralph Eric Thijl Vanstreels, Elisa Cavalcante Pereira et al.. Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025
items.summary: This study investigated potential transmission of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus from infected domestic cats to humans in Los Angeles County following an outbreak linked to consumption of raw animal products. Health authorities conducted a serological survey among people who had been exposed to cats that tested positive for the virus, testing blood samples for H5N1-specific antibodies to detect infections that may not have been identified through standard diagnostic testing. Among those tested, one asymptomatic veterinary professional who had not used respiratory or eye protection during exposures showed serological evidence of H5N1 infection despite never testing positive by conventional methods and reporting no other known risk factors. These findings provide evidence of possible cat-to-human transmission of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b virus, representing a notable spillover event in a domestic setting. The authors emphasize the importance of proper infection control practices in veterinary environments and highlight the value of serosurveys in detecting subclinical influenza A(H5N1) infections that would otherwise go unrecognized.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Aisling Vaughan, Allison Joyce, Elizabeth Traub et al.. Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Evolution of a truncated nucleocapsid protein enhances SARS-CoV-2 fitness by suppressing antiviral responses
items.citation: Rory P. Mulloy, Danyel Evseev, Noga Sharlin et al.. Evolution of a truncated nucleocapsid protein enhances SARS-CoV-2 fitness by suppressing antiviral responses. PLoS Biology. 2026

items.title: Expert Consensus on the Prevention of Secondary Mucormycosis Following Respiratory Viral Infections
items.summary: This paper addressed the growing clinical challenge of secondary mucormycosis occurring after respiratory viral infections, particularly those caused by SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses. A multidisciplinary group of experts was convened to develop a formal consensus document aimed at guiding prevention strategies for this complication. The resulting consensus identifies high-risk populations and provides a set of preventive recommendations organized around four domains: education and training, personal protection, early diagnosis and treatment, and infection control. The document also acknowledges areas where evidence remains limited or contested and proposes directions for future research. Overall, the consensus seeks to systematically optimize prevention practices and raise broader awareness of mucormycosis as a serious secondary complication of respiratory viral disease.
items.citation: Junyan Qu, Xinyao Liu, Min Quan et al.. Expert Consensus on the Prevention of Secondary Mucormycosis Following Respiratory Viral Infections. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Efficacy of the nucleoside analog 4′-Fluorouridine against Nipah virus in the Syrian hamster model
items.citation: Olivier Escaffre, Madison L. Pearson, Terry L. Juelich et al.. Efficacy of the nucleoside analog 4′-Fluorouridine against Nipah virus in the Syrian hamster model. PLoS Pathogens. 2026

items.title: Across-Design Uncertainty in Short Pricing Panels: Evidence from Simulated Price Trajectories
items.summary: This paper investigates a statistical problem that arises when short pricing panels contain many observations but only a limited number of distinct price movements, creating a gap between apparent data richness and true identifying variation. Using synthetic data calibrated to a sparse pricing regime, the authors decompose estimation uncertainty into two components: uncertainty conditional on a single realized price trajectory, and variation in estimation error across alternative trajectories that the same pricing process could have generated. They find that the across-design component—reflecting how results would differ had prices moved differently—dominates total estimation error, accounting for nearly all variance in the gradient-boosted specification, and that conventional within-panel resampling methods fail to capture this component because they condition on only one realized trajectory. The authors characterize across-design dispersion with an empirical power-law relationship involving the number and magnitude of price moves, show that adding geographic units sharing a common price path reduces outcome noise without generating independent identifying variation, and demonstrate that a variance component estimator applied across independently priced units substantially improves confidence interval coverage. The broader implication is that reliable inference in pricing research requires deliberately engineering independent sources of price variation rather than relying on passive accumulation of observations within a fixed panel.
items.citation: Pedro Cadahia Delgado. Across-Design Uncertainty in Short Pricing Panels: Evidence from Simulated Price Trajectories. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Move by Move: Measuring and Steering How LLMs Conduct Psychotherapy
items.summary: This paper investigated how large language models conduct psychotherapy interactions compared to human clinicians, addressing a gap in understanding given the growing use of AI for emotional support. The researchers developed an ontology of ten therapeutic moves grounded in an established clinical inventory, validated by licensed psychologists, and scaled using an automated judging approach that matches expert-level agreement. Applying this framework to real counseling transcripts and model-led sessions, they found that frontier models systematically over-use inquiry at far higher rates than human therapists, neglect psychoeducation, and tend to continue strategies introduced by human clinicians rather than initiating them independently. Exposing the ontology as a set of tools that models could explicitly select approximately halved the deviation from human move distributions and improved turn-level alignment with human therapist behavior by several percentage points, all without any fine-tuning.
items.citation: Afonso Baldo, Hugo Pitorro, Areti Vassilopoulos et al.. Move by Move: Measuring and Steering How LLMs Conduct Psychotherapy. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) in a timely manner, noting that conventional machine learning approaches relying on clinical and laboratory data introduce problematic delays. To overcome this limitation, the authors focused on home monitoring scenarios using only respiratory data collected from daily-use ventilators, avoiding the latency inherent in clinical workflows. They developed a Time-Aware transformer-based model designed to capture both symptom patterns and their temporal progression from ventilator data, generating meaningful patient representations. Experimental results showed that this approach outperformed traditional methods across multiple classification tasks, suggesting it could improve both the speed and accuracy of AECOPD prediction.
items.citation: Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Dongyang Wang et al.. Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Event-Time Confounding Under Bursty Human Dynamics
items.summary: This paper examines a systematic bias that arises when researchers study the effects of user-initiated digital events, such as opening an AI assistant or clicking a recommendation, by measuring activity afterward. The core problem identified is that these events do not occur at random moments but tend to happen during ongoing bursts of user activity, meaning post-event increases in behavior may simply reflect the continuation of a pre-existing episode rather than any causal effect of the event itself. The authors demonstrate this pattern empirically across multiple digital surfaces, showing that activity rises before the event and peaks prior to the chosen time zero, and they validate the bias using known-null timestamps that causally affect nothing yet still show substantially elevated post-event activity compared to a within-user placebo. They formally prove that a single-surface event window cannot disentangle this episode-selection bias from genuine effects without additional assumptions, and they show through simulations that common corrections like user fixed effects and coarse activity matching fail because the confound is within-user and time-varying. To address this, the authors introduce a diagnostic protocol and an open audit tool, arguing that valid causal inference requires comparing similar behavioral episodes with and without the event rather than simply measuring post-event volume.
items.citation: Michael Iannelli, Alan Ai. Event-Time Confounding Under Bursty Human Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A framework for combined epidemiological-genomic inference to improve estimation of household model parameters
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in household transmission modeling: distinguishing within-household from between-household transmission rates is difficult because many different transmission histories can produce identical final outbreak sizes. The authors developed a continuous-time Markov chain framework that expands the model state space to include transmission graphs capturing infection direction and ordering, then incorporated idealized pathogen genomic data to identify which transmission histories are compatible with observed epidemiological outcomes. Through simulation studies, they demonstrated that integrating genomic information substantially concentrates the likelihood surface compared to models relying on epidemiological data alone. Notably, genomic data reduces the correlation between internal and external transmission parameters, eliminating the ridge in the likelihood landscape that reflects their weak identifiability under purely epidemiological approaches. The findings establish that graph-resolved household models can improve transmission inference while remaining analytically and computationally tractable.
items.citation: Golsa Sayyar, Joe Hilton, Thomas House. A framework for combined epidemiological-genomic inference to improve estimation of household model parameters. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CellPath-Bench: A Multidimensional Benchmark for Whole-Slide Cellular Representations in Pathology Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper addresses the gap in evaluation tools for pathology foundation models, specifically their ability to encode and transfer cellular information at the whole-slide level. The authors constructed CellPath-Bench, a benchmark built from spatially aligned hematoxylin and eosin tissue sections paired with Xenium spatial transcriptomics data spanning multiple organs and millions of cells, harmonized into both fine- and coarse-grained cell-type taxonomies. Frozen feature maps from foundation models were sampled at registered nuclear coordinates and evaluated using linear probes to assess how well cell-type information could be decoded from the representations. Two metrics were introduced: Cell Representation Advantage, which quantifies how much better nucleus-anchored features perform compared to patch-level mean pooling within a tissue section, and Cell Representation Transferability, which measures how well cell-type decodability generalizes across sections, datasets, and organs. Benchmarking a large set of pathology-specific and general-purpose foundation models revealed substantial differences among models in both the quality and cross-domain generalizability of their cellular representations, providing a standardized framework for auditing these capabilities.
items.citation: Bokai Zhao, Yiyang Zhang, Hanqing Chao et al.. CellPath-Bench: A Multidimensional Benchmark for Whole-Slide Cellular Representations in Pathology Foundation Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines lateral flow immunoassay technology as a diagnostic platform for viral infectious diseases, with particular emphasis on its potential beyond conventional point-of-care testing. The authors systematically survey recent advances across three domains: signal generation and transduction using diverse nanomaterials spanning colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal approaches; multimodal and multiplex detection strategies for improving sensitivity and throughput; and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation and system optimization. Applications in detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids are comprehensively reviewed alongside current limitations including sensitivity constraints, specificity issues, and practical challenges related to cost and stability. A central argument of the review is that lateral flow immunoassay should be reconceptualized as a point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic surveillance and pandemic preparedness rather than being viewed solely as a simple bedside tool. The authors propose future directions centered on advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection to realize this broader public health potential.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Polydopamine nanoparticle-based colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode lateral flow immunoassay for thromboembolism diagnosis.
items.summary: This paper investigated whether polydopamine nanoparticles could serve as superior signal labels in lateral flow immunoassays to overcome the limited sensitivity and single readout mode associated with conventional gold nanoparticle-based platforms. The researchers constructed a dual-mode lateral flow immunoassay that exploits the high molar extinction coefficient and broadband ultraviolet-to-near-infrared absorption of polydopamine nanoparticles to enable both colorimetric and photothermal detection of two thromboembolism-related biomarkers, thrombomodulin and α₂-plasmin inhibitor-plasmin complex, in clinical serum. The photothermal readout provided substantial sensitivity gains over the colorimetric mode alone, and the platform was validated against clinical reference methods using a set of patient serum samples, demonstrating strong agreement. The authors conclude that this polydopamine nanoparticle-based dual-mode strategy meaningfully advances the sensitivity and reliability of point-of-care lateral flow diagnostics for thrombosis assessment.
items.citation: Yin J, Qiu Y, Nie Y et al.. Polydopamine nanoparticle-based colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode lateral flow immunoassay for thromboembolism diagnosis.. RSC advances. 2026

items.title: A lateral flow microarray immunoassay to detect USUV NS1-specific antibodies in tissues of deceased blackbirds in the Netherlands.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a lateral flow microarray immunoassay (LMIA) could detect Usutu virus (USUTU)-specific antibodies in tissues from deceased Eurasian blackbirds, addressing a gap in current surveillance approaches that focus on live birds and require dedicated laboratory infrastructure. The researchers tested the LMIA against extracts from blood clots, lung, and liver tissues collected from blackbird carcasses found in the Netherlands, using the viral non-structural protein NS1 as a capture antigen. They found that lung tissue extracts showed the strongest trend toward detecting USUV NS1-specific antibodies in RT-PCR-confirmed positive birds, while the assay demonstrated minimal cross-reactivity with the related West Nile virus NS1 antigen. The results establish proof of concept that this LMIA approach can specifically identify USUV antibodies in tissues from deceased birds. The authors propose that such a tool could enable rapid field-based serological screening of both live and dead blackbirds, thereby expanding the scope and practicality of USUV surveillance programs.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. A lateral flow microarray immunoassay to detect USUV NS1-specific antibodies in tissues of deceased blackbirds in the Netherlands.. Virus research. 2026

items.title: Boronate-mediated antibody orientation: a molecular simulation-guided strategy for ultra-sensitive lateral flow immunoassays.
items.summary: This paper investigated how antibody orientation during immobilization affects the sensitivity and consistency of lateral flow immunoassays, addressing the longstanding problem that random antibody attachment leaves many antigen-binding sites inaccessible. The researchers developed a boronate affinity strategy that covalently links boronic acid to cis-diol groups on antibody Fc-region glycans, ensuring that the antigen-binding Fab regions are preferentially exposed, and used molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the binding energetics and conformational stabilization process. Simulations revealed that the boronate-antibody configuration had the most favorable binding energy and achieved rapid conformational stabilization through a sequence of electrostatic guidance followed by hydrogen-bond and covalent bond formation. Experimentally, the oriented immobilization dramatically improved antibody conjugation efficiency, Fab exposure, and functional affinity compared to conventional passive adsorption, and when applied to detecting the mycotoxin zearalenone in corn it achieved a sensitivity several hundred times greater than traditional colloidal gold lateral flow assays, with results validating well against mass spectrometry. The authors conclude that this chemistry-driven, simulation-guided approach to antibody immobilization represents a generalizable framework for improving next-generation rapid diagnostic platforms.
items.citation: Yang Z, Yan X, Yang Z et al.. Boronate-mediated antibody orientation: a molecular simulation-guided strategy for ultra-sensitive lateral flow immunoassays.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.
items.summary: This study evaluated a field-deployable serological assay for detecting arbovirus antibodies in wild birds, focusing on Usutu virus (USUV) and West Nile virus (WNV), which circulate between mosquitoes and avian hosts. The researchers tested a species-independent Lateral Flow Microarray ImmunoAssay (LMIA) capable of simultaneously detecting antibodies against both viruses directly at wild bird capture sites in the Netherlands. Wild birds caught at ringing stations were tested on-site, with a subset also analysed using the gold-standard Focus Reduction Neutralization Test for comparison. The LMIA demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for USUV relative to the gold standard, and successfully detected seroconversion in a Eurasian blackbird, which was independently confirmed. Performance was further assessed against the WHO REASSURED framework for point-of-care diagnostics, where the assay scored highly, supporting its suitability for rapid, multi-analyte, equipment-light surveillance in both routine and resource-limited field settings.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.
items.summary: This study addressed a key limitation of conventional lateral flow immunoassay diagnostics, namely the random orientation of antibodies on colloidal gold nanoparticles that reduces antigen-binding efficiency. The researchers developed a one-pot, room-temperature synthesis method to produce phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles at large scale, yielding uniform, monodisperse particles in large batch volumes within minutes without the harsh high-temperature conditions typically required. These nanoparticles exploit boronate-affinity interactions with carbohydrate moieties on antibody Fc fragments to achieve oriented, site-directed antibody immobilization rather than random physical adsorption. When tested in a lateral flow assay for fecal occult blood detection, the functionalized nanoparticles delivered dramatically improved sensitivity compared to conventional citrate-capped gold nanoparticle probes. The authors conclude that this scalable, cost-effective nanoplatform holds strong potential for clinical translation in high-sensitivity point-of-care diagnostics.
items.citation: Xu J, Li Q, Lu B et al.. Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.. Colloids and surfaces. B, Biointerfaces. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines biosensing technologies designed for the rapid and accurate detection of priority foodborne pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, with relevance to both food safety and clinical healthcare applications. The authors survey advances across electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, paying particular attention to how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity and specificity in complex food matrices. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transforms conventional sensors into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically assesses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular multi-pathogen detection panels, blockchain-based data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as essential steps toward deployable, regulation-ready food safety monitoring systems.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review paper examined the dual nature of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they serve as essential signaling molecules at physiological levels but drive disease when produced excessively or in a dysregulated manner. The authors synthesized current knowledge on the major types, sources, and physiological functions of reactive oxygen species, alongside the molecular pathways through which redox imbalance causes cellular damage and signaling dysregulation. The review also critically evaluated contemporary and emerging detection methods for measuring oxidative stress, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging approaches. The contribution of oxidative stress to major diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory conditions was examined in depth. The authors conclude by outlining future directions in precision redox medicine, emphasizing targeted antioxidant-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies informed by improved detection technologies and a deeper mechanistic understanding of redox biology.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Spherical Nucleic Acids: Turning Synthetic Advances and Fundamental Discovery into Translational Breakthroughs in Chemistry, Materials Development, Biology, and Medicine
items.summary: Spherical nucleic acids (SNAs) are nanoconstructs comprising a nanoparticle core densely coated with a radially oriented oligonucleotide shell, and this review uses their roughly thirty-year development as a case study in how synthetic control and fundamental discovery drive translational breakthroughs. The authors trace the evolution of SNAs from their origins as gold nanoparticle–DNA conjugates through the establishment of broad synthetic toolkits that now encompass dozens of SNA classes and related anisotropic programmable atom equivalents. Key discoveries showed that the dense, radial nucleic acid architecture confers distinctive properties—including enhanced binding affinity to complementary DNA, resistance to enzymatic degradation, reduced immune activation, and transfection-agent-free cellular uptake—that define SNAs as a distinct materials class with well-articulated design rules. These properties have been leveraged across biomedical applications including intracellular probes, gene regulation tools, vaccines, and CRISPR-coupled gene editing platforms, while in parallel, sequence-specific DNA interactions among SNAs have enabled the assembly of three-dimensional colloidal crystals with programmable lattice symmetries and compositions that yield metamaterials with properties such as negative refractive indices and shape memory. The review argues that SNAs provide a generalizable framework illustrating how mastery of nanoscale synthesis and mechanistic understanding can catalyze innovation spanning chemistry, materials science, biology, and medicine.
items.citation: Connor M. Forsyth, Rachel R. Chan, Tanner D. Fink et al.. Spherical Nucleic Acids: Turning Synthetic Advances and Fundamental Discovery into Translational Breakthroughs in Chemistry, Materials Development, Biology, and Medicine. Accounts of Chemical Research. 2026

items.title: Histoplasmosis: a missing piece in the global efforts to end HIV deaths
items.citation: Alessandro C Pasqualotto, Thuy Vi Le, Tarsila Vieceli et al.. Histoplasmosis: a missing piece in the global efforts to end HIV deaths. The Lancet HIV. 2026

items.title: Rethinking Extracellular Vesicle Signaling
items.summary: This paper challenges the prevailing view of how extracellular vesicles communicate between cells. Conventionally, extracellular vesicle signaling has been understood primarily as a process in which vesicles are internalized by a recipient cell and release their internal cargo into the cytoplasm. The authors propose two alternative surface-binding mechanisms — termed "bind-and-stay" and "bind-and-leave" — in which vesicles signal through interactions at the cell surface without being internalized. The "bind-and-leave" mode is particularly significant because it implies that a single vesicle can transiently bind and activate signaling in multiple successive cells, overturning the conventional "one-vesicle-one-cell" model. The paper offers a forward-looking perspective on the relative efficiency of these signaling modes and identifies experimental techniques that could be used to investigate them, with implications for both fundamental cell biology and the development of extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics.
items.citation: Wojciech Chrzanowski, Joy Wolfram. Rethinking Extracellular Vesicle Signaling. Advanced Materials. 2026

items.title: Mechanistic advances in microbial nanobiotechnology and their applications in sustainable agriculture, environment and biomedicine
items.summary: This review examines the field of microbial nanobiotechnology, which combines microbiology and nanotechnology to produce nanoparticles using microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and algae through environmentally friendly biochemical pathways. The paper surveys the tools, applications, and challenges associated with these biogenic nanoparticles, which can be tailored in size, shape, and functional properties. Applications discussed span biomedicine—including targeted drug delivery, imaging, and antimicrobial treatments—as well as environmental remediation such as wastewater treatment and pollution control, and industrial uses including agriculture and energy production. The review also highlights how genetic engineering and synthetic biology have advanced nanoparticle synthesis and characterization, while identifying persistent challenges around scalability, biosafety, regulatory frameworks, and ethical concerns. The authors conclude that overcoming these barriers through multidisciplinary collaboration will be essential for translating microbial nanobiotechnology from laboratory research into commercial solutions addressing global health, environmental, and industrial challenges.
items.citation: Mir Sajad Rabani, Meenakshi Shrivastav, Mudasir Fayaz et al.. Mechanistic advances in microbial nanobiotechnology and their applications in sustainable agriculture, environment and biomedicine. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: VIALS: A Benchmark for Visual Interpretation of Artifacts in the Life Sciences
items.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark designed to evaluate how well vision-language models can interpret the kinds of visual artifacts that life scientists routinely encounter in professional research settings, such as gel blots, microscopy images, plasmid maps, flow cytometry plots, and molecular structures. The benchmark consists of visual question-answering tasks drawn from realistic biotech industry workflows rather than polished figures from publications or textbooks. The authors tested frontier vision-language models on these tasks and found that, despite their ability to describe natural images fluently, these models perform poorly on scientific image interpretation, revealing deficits in domain knowledge and domain-specific visual reasoning. By contrast, scientists with relevant expertise found the same tasks straightforward. The authors argue that this gap represents a meaningful obstacle to deploying AI effectively in professional life sciences contexts, where interpreting such visual artifacts is central to scientific reasoning and decision-making.
items.citation: Elaine Lau, Thanuka Udumulla, Lee Izhaki-Tavor et al.. VIALS: A Benchmark for Visual Interpretation of Artifacts in the Life Sciences. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AI with Authority, from Application to Silicon
items.summary: This paper investigated whether generative AI agents, guided by a structured verification discipline, could autonomously carry out a complete hardware design and verification project from application software down to physical silicon. A single researcher directed a fleet of AI agents over five weeks using consumer AI subscriptions, producing a verified compiler, executive, and a RISC-V processor that was fabricated through a community silicon shuttle, with no human-written register-transfer logic and no human review of individual proofs. The methodology, called the Salt method, uses a formal proof kernel as an incorruptible arbiter so that mathematical claims between agents must pass machine verification before being accepted, with human attention restricted to high-level statements and design decisions rather than proof details. Verification was maintained continuously from the formal proof checker through to equivalence checking at the silicon boundary, and the project recorded a detailed error ledger showing numerous catches with zero incorrect proofs reaching the final record. The authors claim this demonstrates that machine verification, far from being a costly overhead, becomes an essential productivity enabler when AI agents operate at scale.
items.citation: Jason Hickey. AI with Authority, from Application to Silicon. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Efficient Event Generation for High-Multiplicity LHC Processes: An End-to-End GPU Workflow with Normalizing Flows
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of generating large samples of unweighted particle collision events for high-multiplicity processes at the Large Hadron Collider, where expensive matrix-element evaluations and low unweighting efficiencies create significant bottlenecks. The authors developed the first end-to-end GPU-resident event-generation workflow by integrating normalizing flow neural networks with the parton-level event generator Pepper, keeping all data transfers within device memory to minimize overhead.
