The system employs helicity-conditioned coupling flows trained with online updates and sample replay, and the authors compared subprocess-specific flows against grouped conditional flows that share parameters across related partonic subprocesses. Benchmarked across several complex processes involving multiple jets, top-quark pairs, and electroweak final states, the workflow was shown to produce billion-event samples on a small GPU cluster. The approach achieves end-to-end speedups of up to two orders of magnitude compared to standalone event generation, reducing what would otherwise be a multi-week computation to less than a day and offering a practical path toward alleviating the Monte Carlo statistics bottleneck in collider physics.
items.citation: Enrico Bothmann, Joshua Isaacson, Claudius Krause et al.. Efficient Event Generation for High-Multiplicity LHC Processes: An End-to-End GPU Workflow with Normalizing Flows. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Maxwell's Demon in Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Cooling Information Flow and Entropy Balance
items.summary: This paper examines the thermodynamic and information-theoretic interpretation of Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms by drawing an analogy with Maxwell's Demon. The authors identify the acceptance-rejection module of these algorithms as the Demon: it measures a proposed transition, stores the outcome in a single decision bit, and uses that information to direct probability currents toward the target distribution. The decision bit carries genuine Shannon mutual information about the proposal, but only its directional component contributes to what the authors term a cooling information flow. A central result is a decomposition of the relative-entropy relaxation rate into a cooling information flow term and an entropy production term, cleanly separating the useful convergence toward the target distribution from irreversible housekeeping circulation present in nonreversible chains. This framework provides a unified information-theoretic account of how acceptance-rejection mechanisms drive sampling algorithms toward equilibrium.
items.citation: Masayuki Ohzeki. Maxwell's Demon in Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Cooling Information Flow and Entropy Balance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: This paper examines the deployment of autonomous AI diagnostic agents across eHealth platforms in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on the governance and ethical gaps that arise when such systems operate without mandatory real-time human review. The authors identify a structural accountability gap rooted in a patient-centered analysis, arguing that existing frameworks for AI transparency and explainability are predominantly clinician-centered and assume regulatory conditions that do not reflect low-resource settings. Drawing on documented deployment cases involving tuberculosis detection, diabetic retinopathy screening, and mobile health chatbot triage across Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana, the paper demonstrates that these gaps are already manifest in active real-world systems. In response, the authors synthesize literature on informed consent, algorithmic accountability, and explainable AI to propose three foundational principles: agent-aware informed consent, human override as a structural requirement, and contextually adapted explainability. These principles are framed as a practical minimum standard for developers, health administrators, and policymakers operating in contexts where formal AI regulation remains underdeveloped.
items.citation: Percy Brown, Kweku Yamoah. Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diversity of Galaxy Centers from Small-Scale Isocurvature
items.summary: This paper investigates whether variations in dark matter composition at galactic centers could explain the observed diversity of galaxy central density profiles, particularly the range of cusp-like and core-like structures seen across galaxies. The authors propose a scenario in which a subdominant ultralight dark matter component carries large-amplitude small-scale isocurvature perturbations, and they test this idea using N-body simulations. They find that while nonlinear gravitational evolution tends to homogenize the ultralight dark matter fraction on large galactic scales, the large initial fluctuations seed early potential wells that preferentially concentrate ultralight dark matter at halo centers. Even when the cosmological abundance of ultralight dark matter is small, it can come to dominate the central regions of small halos, extending well beyond a percent of the virial radius. This central segregation produces stochastic halo-to-halo variation in central dark matter composition, offering a potential explanation for the observed diversity of galaxy centers without requiring ultralight dark matter to be the dominant component of dark matter overall.
items.citation: Jessica N. Lopez-Sanchez, Wen Yin. Diversity of Galaxy Centers from Small-Scale Isocurvature. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This study describes the design and enrollment procedures for an ongoing prospective mixed-methods investigation examining whether point-of-care nucleic acid tests could improve HIV detection and viral load monitoring in the United States. The rationale is that such tests offer shorter window periods than serologic point-of-care tests and faster turnaround than laboratory-based nucleic acid testing, potentially benefiting both early diagnosis and real-time management of people living with HIV. The study enrolled participants across a hospital-based clinic and a community LGBTQ+ center in Seattle, administering qualitative and semiquantitative whole-blood point-of-care nucleic acid tests alongside standard laboratory comparators, and also incorporated a randomized clinical trial arm, acceptability surveys, in-depth interviews, and time-and-motion workflow observations. Enrollment was completed with hundreds of participants spanning those seeking HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis, or post-exposure prophylaxis, as well as people already living with HIV. Because data analysis has not yet been conducted, the abstract reports only that results on test performance, clinical outcomes, acceptability, and workflow impact are anticipated in future publications.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.
items.summary: This study examined whether pharmacological measures of tenofovir adherence could predict future HIV viremia in people with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy in South Africa. Researchers compared three adherence metrics — a point-of-care urine tenofovir antibody-based assay, quantitative urine tenofovir measured by liquid-chromatography-mass-spectrometry, and tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots — and assessed their associations with both current and subsequent viral load outcomes using logistic regression. Among the participants studied, higher tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots were significantly and negatively associated with viremia at twenty-four weeks, while neither the point-of-care urine assay nor quantitative urine tenofovir showed a statistically significant association with future viral load. Participants with undetectable point-of-care urine tenofovir were more likely to be viremic at enrollment and to have lower CD4 counts, suggesting this result may reflect recent treatment initiation rather than long-term non-adherence. The findings indicate that dried blood spot tenofovir-diphosphate measurement is the most useful of the three measures for identifying patients at risk of future viremia and potentially guiding targeted adherence interventions.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Bodley N, Govender K, Moodley P et al.. Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the longstanding question in exercise immunology of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper structured opposing arguments around four contested issues: whether athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond confounding factors such as sleep disruption, anxiety, travel, and nutritional deficits, whether commonly used biomarkers and in vitro data reliably reflect immune health under conditions of arduous training, and whether the existing scientific evidence is sufficiently robust to support claims about exercise-induced immune suppression. There is broad agreement that regular moderate-intensity exercise is beneficial for immune defense, particularly in older adults and those with chronic disease, while high infection burden among elite athletes and military personnel has historically supported the view that extreme exercise suppresses immunity. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in nature, but whether exercise per se is an independent causative factor of increased infection risk remains unresolved. The article calls for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle the specific contribution of exercise from the many co-occurring stressors in athletic and military populations.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Sepsis
items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review paper examines exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by transporting bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids, with a focus on the molecular mechanisms governing their biogenesis, cargo loading, and functional heterogeneity. The authors synthesize current understanding of the regulatory machinery involved—including ESCRT complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications—and survey state-of-the-art omics platforms and machine learning tools used to characterize exosomal content. The review evaluates the diagnostic utility of exosomes as liquid biopsy biomarkers across cancer, metabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases, while also addressing their therapeutic applications in drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, including evidence from ongoing clinical trials. The authors identify persistent translational barriers such as isolation protocol variability, cargo inconsistency, targeting specificity, and regulatory constraints. They conclude by proposing a forward-looking framework integrating basic biology, bioengineering, and clinical translation—incorporating emerging approaches such as synthetic exosome mimetics and AI-driven diagnostics—to advance exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients
items.summary: These two open-label randomized platform trials investigated whether nirmatrelvir–ritonavir reduces hospitalization or death in higher-risk outpatients with COVID-19 who were predominantly vaccinated or had prior natural immunity, a population not well studied in earlier trials of the drug. Adults aged fifty or older, or younger adults with relevant comorbidities, who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and had been symptomatic for five days or fewer were randomly assigned to receive nirmatrelvir–ritonavir plus usual care or usual care alone. Neither trial demonstrated a statistically meaningful reduction in the primary outcome of hospitalization or death within twenty-eight days in the nirmatrelvir–ritonavir group compared with usual care. Although a viral load substudy confirmed that the drug did reduce viral replication by the end of treatment, this biological effect did not translate into a clinical benefit for this vaccinated, higher-risk population. The findings suggest that nirmatrelvir–ritonavir does not reduce severe outcomes in higher-risk individuals who have prior immunity through vaccination or natural infection.
items.citation: Christopher C. Butler, Andrew Pinto, Victoria Harris et al.. Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors analyze multiomics approaches spanning genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiling in combination with deep learning methodologies to understand how these tools collectively illuminate disease mechanisms at a molecular level. The review covers applications across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Case studies in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate the practical potential of this convergence. The authors conclude that while challenges such as data harmonization, reproducibility, and algorithmic bias remain, the fusion of multiomics and artificial intelligence opens significant new pathways for therapeutic innovation and bench-to-clinic translation.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: 2025 Inborn errors of immunity practice parameter
items.citation: Jordan S. Orange, Javier Chinen, Caroline C. Horner et al.. 2025 Inborn errors of immunity practice parameter. Annals of Allergy Asthma & Immunology. 2026

items.title: SPARCL: Spectral Partitioned Analytic Continual Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates why analytic continual learning methods, which use closed-form recursive solvers rather than gradient-based optimization, still experience performance drift on previously learned classes during class-incremental learning. The authors identify the underlying mechanism as spectral interference, wherein new task data that projects onto dominant eigendirections of the shared inverse autocorrelation operator dilutes the spectrum and perturbs old-class predictions even without revisiting old labels. To address this, they propose SPARCL, which decomposes the running autocorrelation matrix into a high-energy core subspace and a residual complement, freezing old-class classifier components within the core while updating only the residual block via recursive least squares with optional random-projection expansion. This design provides a provable invariance guarantee for the core contribution to old-class logits. Evaluated across multiple benchmark datasets using a frozen vision transformer backbone, SPARCL substantially closes the performance gap between classical analytic learners and strong representation-matching approaches, and is shown to be complementary to existing feature-decorrelation methods.
items.citation: James Hartley, Zeropy Surio, Daniel Whitmore et al.. SPARCL: Spectral Partitioned Analytic Continual Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Loadability Limits Under Periodic Load Forcing
items.summary: This paper examines how the loadability limit of a power system changes when part of the demand varies periodically, as is characteristic of data-center loads, rather than remaining constant. The authors extend the classical static loadability analysis—based on finding when equilibrium equations lose their solution—to the dynamic setting by analyzing fixed points of the period map for forced periodic orbits. They show that at the dynamic loadability limit, the monodromy matrix acquires a Floquet multiplier at unity, meaning the generic instability is a cyclic fold of the periodic orbit rather than the saddle-node bifurcation of equilibria that characterizes voltage collapse. As a consequence, the loadability limit becomes a function of the forcing frequency, an effect that static analysis cannot capture. On a test system, the effective stability margin is shown to shrink dramatically near the swing frequency, the dominant instability mechanism shifts from voltage collapse to a rotor-angle fold, and transient cold-start failures can occur even at amplitudes where a stable periodic orbit exists.
items.citation: Maitraya Avadhut Desai, Gustavo Valverde, Gabriela Hug. Loadability Limits Under Periodic Load Forcing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SPICE: Speculative Prefetching with Low-Rank Expert Surrogates and Heterogeneous Orchestration for MoE Inference Acceleration
items.summary: This paper investigates the inference bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts large language models that arises when expert parameters exceed GPU memory, forcing costly data transfers across the PCIe bus from host to device. The authors developed SPICE, a speculative prefetching framework that uses a lightweight draft model to predict which experts will be needed and prefetches them ahead of time using a confidence-aware adaptive lookahead strategy. When predictions miss, the system applies a heterogeneous recovery strategy: low-confidence misses are approximated using low-rank surrogate experts co-located with the shared expert on the GPU, while higher-stakes misses requiring exact computation are offloaded asynchronously to the CPU in parallel with ongoing GPU work. Evaluated across two MoE model architectures and multiple GPU platforms, SPICE achieved substantial speedups in time per output token with minimal degradation in output quality. The work demonstrates that efficient MoE offloading depends not only on accurate expert prediction but also on intelligently triaging prediction failures by deciding whether to approximate, recover exactly, and where to execute residual computation.
items.citation: Yongxiang Lyu, Ning Li, Bonian Jia. SPICE: Speculative Prefetching with Low-Rank Expert Surrogates and Heterogeneous Orchestration for MoE Inference Acceleration. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Identification of the length scale parameter of simplified strain gradient elasticity from standard Mode I fracture tests
items.summary: This paper investigates how to determine the length scale parameter that appears in simplified strain gradient elasticity theory, which extends classical elasticity by incorporating microstructural effects through an additional material constant. The authors conducted precise numerical simulations within the strain gradient elasticity framework for three standard fracture mechanics test configurations under pure Mode I loading conditions. For brittle materials, they derived an explicit closed-form expression relating the length scale parameter to the classical fracture toughness and ultimate tensile strength, showing that this calibration makes the fracture load predictions of strain gradient elasticity consistent with those of classical linear elastic fracture mechanics for sufficiently long cracks while avoiding stress singularities at crack tips. For quasi-brittle materials, they developed regression relations capturing the size effect on strength, which is traditionally addressed through nonlinear fracture mechanics but emerges naturally within the strain gradient elasticity framework. The approach was validated against experimental data for chopped fiber composites and quasi-brittle ceramics of varying porosity, demonstrating practical applicability of the identification procedure.
items.citation: Yury Solyaev, Kirill Shelkov, Pavel Polyakov. Identification of the length scale parameter of simplified strain gradient elasticity from standard Mode I fracture tests. arXiv. 2026

items.title: From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation
items.summary: This paper addresses limitations of current generative recommendation systems, which represent items using multi-level residual quantization into sequences of Semantic IDs, leading to high autoregressive decoding costs, sparse hierarchical code spaces, and misalignment with shifting item distributions over time. The authors propose replacing multi-level residual codes with a single large semantic codebook that assigns each item one semantic token plus a separate collaborative token to handle collisions, dramatically shortening the ID sequence. To keep representations current, they introduce an exposure-aware dynamic update mechanism combining temporal weight decay, exponential moving-average updates, and an exposure-weighted penalty that discourages unnecessary ID reassignment. They also develop an offline evaluation framework to assess representation quality, code utilization, collision rates, and temporal stability. The proposed approach substantially improves ranking metrics on public datasets, reduces autoregressive decoding compute by roughly half while increasing throughput, and yields meaningful gains in a production online experiment.
items.citation: Tianlu Xie, Xin Ku, Mingjie Sun et al.. From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Generalizing Soft Tissue Deformation and Force Prediction Across Material Stiffness and Geometry
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately simulating soft tissue behavior in real time for applications such as surgical training and haptic feedback, where existing learning-based approaches fail to generalize across different tissue stiffnesses or geometries. The researchers systematically calibrated hyperelastic constitutive models within the SOFA simulation framework using gravity-loaded silicone beams spanning a range of stiffnesses, then used these calibrated simulations as training data. They developed a softness-conditioned equivariant graph neural network capable of predicting both deformation and contact forces across multiple tissue types and geometries not seen during training. The model achieves sub-millimeter deformation accuracy at near-real-time inference speeds, demonstrating strong generalization. A key finding is that the quality of force prediction is directly dependent on the consistency of the upstream constitutive model calibration, highlighting the importance of rigorous model selection guidance across stiffness levels.
items.citation: Madina Kojanazarova, Sidaty El Hadramy, Philippe C. Cattin. Generalizing Soft Tissue Deformation and Force Prediction Across Material Stiffness and Geometry. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Sustainability of the Effects of Linkage Case Management on Posthospitalization HIV Outcomes: The Daraja Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: The Daraja randomized clinical trial investigated whether linkage case management could produce lasting improvements in HIV-related outcomes among people with HIV who had been hospitalized. Researchers followed trial participants for an additional year beyond the primary endpoint to assess whether intervention effects were sustained through two years after hospital discharge. Outcomes of interest included continuity in HIV care, antiretroviral therapy adherence, and viral load suppression measured at both the one-year and two-year timepoints. Participants who received the linkage case management intervention consistently outperformed those receiving standard care across all three outcomes, with meaningful differences persisting through the full two-year follow-up period. A notable proportion of control participants remained untreated even at two years, underscoring the durable benefit of the intervention on clinic linkage, treatment initiation, and viral suppression among hospitalized people with HIV.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Willkens M, Issarow B, Kisigo GA et al.. Brief Report: Sustainability of the Effects of Linkage Case Management on Posthospitalization HIV Outcomes: The Daraja Randomized Clinical Trial.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: New to cohort, not new to care: leveraging historical data in HIV clinical cohorts in the United States.
items.summary: This paper examined how to distinguish people newly entering HIV care from those transferring from prior care within United States clinical cohort studies, a distinction important for research validity. The researchers analyzed five types of historical HIV data — antiretroviral therapy prescriptions, CD4 counts, viral loads, suppressed viral load at enrollment, and AIDS-defining conditions — across cohorts participating in a large North American collaboration spanning over two decades. They developed an algorithm to classify participants as new to care, transfers, re-engagements after a care gap, or previously in care with unknown transfer status. They found that the proportion of participants transferring into cohorts grew substantially over time while those truly new to care declined, and that historical antiretroviral prescriptions and suppressed viral load at enrollment became increasingly useful data types for identifying prior care experience, particularly after treatment guidelines expanded. The authors recommend that HIV cohorts systematically collect all five data types and adapt their classification algorithm to improve the accuracy of identifying participants who are genuinely new to HIV care.
items.citation: Haw NJL, Hogan B, Humes E et al.. New to cohort, not new to care: leveraging historical data in HIV clinical cohorts in the United States.. American journal of epidemiology. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of a field-deployable iiPCR platform and viral load dynamics of MPXV Clade IIb in a cohort with high prevalence of HIV.
items.summary: This study evaluated a field-deployable insulated isothermal PCR platform as an alternative to conventional quantitative PCR for diagnosing Mpox caused by MPXV Clade IIb, with particular attention to performance in a cohort with high HIV prevalence. Researchers prospectively enrolled confirmed Mpox patients, testing multiple specimen types with both the portable iiPCR system and reference qPCR, while also assessing viral load dynamics across specimen types and time since symptom onset. The iiPCR system matched qPCR in analytical sensitivity and showed complete qualitative concordance, with lesion-derived specimens yielding the highest detection rates and lowest cycle threshold values, while non-lesion specimens were more variable. Among people living with HIV who were receiving antiretroviral therapy and had preserved immune function, no differences in diagnostic performance were observed compared to HIV-negative individuals. The findings support the potential of this portable iiPCR platform for decentralized Mpox testing, particularly when lesion specimens are available.
items.citation: Liu LT, Chen CJ, Lin PC et al.. Diagnostic performance of a field-deployable iiPCR platform and viral load dynamics of MPXV Clade IIb in a cohort with high prevalence of HIV.. Annals of medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care urine tenofovir test, and associations between metrics of tenofovir use and treatment outcomes in a community ART programme
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a point-of-care urine tenofovir assay and examined how urine tenofovir and dried blood spot tenofovir diphosphate concentrations relate to viral load suppression and retention in care within a South African community antiretroviral therapy programme. Researchers measured tenofovir concentrations using laboratory-based liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry as a reference standard, comparing results against the point-of-care assay, while also assessing associations between these adherence biomarkers and clinical outcomes. The point-of-care assay showed high sensitivity but only moderate specificity for detecting tenofovir above the manufacturer-recommended threshold. The vast majority of participants without detectable viraemia had positive tenofovir results by both methods, suggesting good concordance between adherence biomarkers and viral suppression in this population, though the study was limited in its ability to draw firm conclusions due to the very small number of participants with viraemia. Neither the point-of-care urine tenofovir assay nor dried blood spot tenofovir diphosphate concentrations were associated with retention in care at sixteen weeks following enrolment.
items.citation: Naidu L, Tlhaku K, Govender K et al.. Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care urine tenofovir test, and associations between metrics of tenofovir use and treatment outcomes in a community ART programme. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *P. vivax* co-circulate, and where conventional HRP2-based tests are undermined by low parasite densities and gene deletions. Febrile patients attending health facilities during peak transmission season were tested using the new Bioline Malaria multi-antigen RDT, alongside expert microscopy and quantitative PCR as reference standards. The multi-antigen RDT performed well against microscopy, achieving high sensitivity and specificity with near-perfect agreement, but sensitivity dropped notably when qPCR served as the reference, revealing that submicroscopic, low-density infections were frequently missed. qPCR detected the highest overall prevalence and identified more species-specific and mixed infections than either RDT or microscopy. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is clinically useful for routine diagnosis, more sensitive tools are needed for malaria surveillance and elimination efforts in co-endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.
items.summary: This study investigated circulating arboviruses in Haiti during a period when security concerns had disrupted conventional surveillance efforts. Researchers extracted nucleic acids from discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes collected from febrile patients at healthcare centers across two Haitian departments, then applied a series of real-time PCR assays targeting flaviviruses, alphaviruses, and Oropouche virus, followed by next-generation sequencing and phylogenetic analysis on positive samples. The dominant finding was dengue virus serotype three in samples collected in a single year, with phylogenetic analysis placing these sequences within a broader regional outbreak circulating across the Caribbean and Americas at that time. No evidence of alphavirus or Oropouche virus infections was detected in the subset of samples tested. The study concludes that discarded malaria rapid diagnostic tests represent a practical and valuable surveillance tool in resource-limited or politically unstable settings, capable of supporting both pathogen detection and genomic characterization.
items.citation: Matulis GA, Smith HP, Hall G et al.. Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: Sepsis
items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring
items.summary: This paper presents an integrated telehealth monitoring framework that combines IoT sensor technology with cloud-based artificial intelligence to enable continuous, real-time health surveillance for elderly and chronically ill patients. The system uses the ZigBee wireless protocol to transmit physiological data — including heart rate, body temperature, and blood oxygen levels — from wearable sensors to a centralized processing unit with low power consumption and minimal latency. Multiple machine learning algorithms, including random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression, were applied to detect health anomalies, with the random forest model achieving particularly high accuracy and perfect recall to minimize false negatives. Testing in a real-world care facility demonstrated very low transmission delay and low power consumption, supporting long-term deployment suitability. The authors claim their modular, scalable system addresses key limitations of existing telehealth solutions — such as high latency, false alarms, and poor integration — while reducing burden on healthcare providers and improving patient autonomy.
items.citation: B. V. Ravi Kumar, Mohammad Shahnawaz Shaikh. ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring. Emerging Science Journal. 2026

items.title: Biosynthesis of cinchona alkaloids
items.summary: This paper investigated the biosynthetic pathway by which cinchona plants produce alkaloids such as quinine and cinchonidine, compounds of major pharmaceutical and chemical importance whose plant-based synthesis has remained poorly understood. Using a combination of isotopic labelling, gene silencing, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and comparative transcriptomics, the researchers identified the genes responsible for constructing the characteristic quinoline-quinuclidine scaffold of these alkaloids, revealing several unexpected enzymatic transformations including an unusual cyclization reaction that generates a previously unreported quaternary amine intermediate. When these genes were heterologously expressed in *Nicotiana benthamiana*, the plant host successfully produced cinchona alkaloid scaffold intermediates, and the system could also convert non-native halogenated substrates into novel alkaloid analogues. These findings resolve a long-standing mystery in plant biochemistry and open avenues for producing cinchona alkaloids and their derivatives through metabolic engineering.
items.citation: Blaise Kimbadi Lombe, Tingan Zhou, Gyumin Kang et al.. Biosynthesis of cinchona alkaloids. Nature. 2026

items.title: Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission
items.citation: Hedvig Hricak, Zachary J. Ward, Fabio Ynoe Moraes et al.. Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission. The Lancet Oncology. 2026

items.title: Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare
items.summary: This paper evaluated the safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system embedded in electronic medical records across primary care clinics in Kenya. Trained physicians retrospectively reviewed over a thousand patient encounter records to assess hallucination rates, guideline adherence, and the presence of harmful or beneficial recommendations. The system rarely hallucinated and its guidance aligned with local clinical guidelines in nearly all cases, yet clinicians frequently declined to modify their documentation based on its suggestions. Critically, actively harmful recommendations from the system appeared in a meaningful proportion of encounters, and when clinicians did selectively adopt suggestions, they were more likely to incorporate harmful outputs than to accept beneficial ones that could have mitigated pre-existing risks in their notes. The authors conclude that while the tool shows promise for supporting quality improvement in African primary healthcare, the imbalanced uptake of harmful versus beneficial outputs highlights an urgent need for usability improvements, locally tailored safety guardrails, and prospective trials to establish patient-level benefit.
items.citation: Ambrose Agweyu, Paul Mwaniki, Wilkister Musau et al.. Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: Multi-epitope vaccine against nucleoprotein and envelopment polyprotein of Batai orthobunyavirus using molecular docking and molecular dynamics studies
items.citation: Muhammad Naveed, Muhammad Asim, Adeeba Ali et al.. Multi-epitope vaccine against nucleoprotein and envelopment polyprotein of Batai orthobunyavirus using molecular docking and molecular dynamics studies. Scientific Reports. 2026

items.title: Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution
items.summary: This paper investigates the reliability gap between natural-language workflows and the software-like behavior expected when AI agents execute them, focusing on problems such as implicit data dependencies and difficulty following complex branching instructions. The authors developed Artic, a compiler that transforms natural-language workflows into structured artifact-driven representations where each step explicitly declares its inputs and outputs, enforces constraints on produced artifacts, and uses explicit control flow transfers. The compiler also identifies steps with excessive state dependencies or complex control logic and refines them through constrained optimization, while validating the transformation using decomposed faithfulness checks and scenario-based dry runs. Evaluated on a substantial collection of real-world domain workflow problem instances, Artic substantially improved task resolution rates compared to executing the original text workflows. The compiled workflows also demonstrated markedly greater consistency when tested across different language models and across repeated executions of the same workflow.
items.citation: Xiangzhe Xu, Hanxi Guo, Guangyu Shen et al.. Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation
items.summary: This paper introduces Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), a framework that encodes anatomical knowledge into deep learning models either as soft penalty terms in the loss function or as hard architectural constraints that make anatomically impossible predictions structurally unachievable. The approach is developed for a clinical problem with limited data availability: predicting how the aortoiliac arterial tree deforms when a stiff guidewire is inserted endoluminally, a deformation relevant to modern aortic surgery and autonomous endovascular navigation. The authors represent vessel centerlines and wire paths as curves of frames in the Lie group SE(3), coupling a Cosserat-rod model of the wire to the vessel through a contact inequality constraint, with the prediction arising as a constrained minimizer of coupled elastic energy. Training supervision is formulated as a Wasserstein-2 optimal-transport loss between predicted angiographic projections and observed two-dimensional angiograms, enabling three-dimensional predictions to be learned from two-dimensional imaging. Importantly, no network is actually trained in this work; the paper establishes and verifies the mathematical and mechanical framework, with future work planned to apply the approach to real computed tomography data and assess whether anatomical priors improve accuracy and reduce data requirements.
items.citation: David P. Stonko. Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: This paper examines the ethical and governance challenges arising from the deployment of autonomous AI diagnostic agents on eHealth platforms in sub-Saharan Africa, where such systems analyze patient clinical data and produce diagnostic or triage outputs without mandatory real-time human oversight. The authors argue that existing accountability and explainability frameworks are predominantly clinician-centered and presuppose regulatory conditions that do not exist in low-resource settings, leaving a structural gap in patient awareness and informed consent. Drawing on documented deployment cases involving tuberculosis detection, diabetic retinopathy screening, and mobile chatbot triage across Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana, the paper demonstrates that these accountability deficits are already manifest in active real-world deployments. In response, the authors propose three foundational principles—agent-aware informed consent, mandatory human override as a structural requirement, and contextually adapted explainability—intended to establish a practical minimum governance standard for developers, health administrators, and policymakers operating where formal AI regulation remains nascent.
items.citation: Percy Brown, Kweku Yamoah. Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) in a timely manner, noting that conventional machine learning approaches relying on clinical and laboratory data introduce problematic delays. To overcome this, the authors developed a Time-Aware transformer-based model designed for home monitoring scenarios that relies solely on respiratory data collected from daily-use ventilators. The model generates patient representations that capture both symptom patterns and their temporal progression within the ventilator data stream. Experimental results showed that the Time-Aware transformer approach outperformed traditional methods across multiple classification tasks, suggesting it can improve both the speed and accuracy of AECOPD prediction.
items.citation: Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Dongyang Wang et al.. Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hypothesis testing between quantum ensembles
items.summary: This paper investigates the problem of distinguishing between two quantum state ensembles, which are collections of quantum states accompanied by classical labels and carry operational information beyond what is captured by their average density operators. The authors develop a framework for binary hypothesis testing between finite quantum ensembles, carefully accounting for the label-permutation invariance that distinguishes ensembles from classical-quantum states. By analyzing observed label patterns, they show that the relevant statistical object is a hierarchy of power-weighted ensemble moments, from which they derive the Bayes-optimal measurement and exact finite-sample error probabilities. In the many-sample regime, they obtain Chernoff-type error exponents and find that discrimination difficulty is governed by the full moment hierarchy up to the sample size. Applying these results to optical communication and quantum designs, they establish that for pure-state designs with large design order, the optimal discrimination exponent decays as the inverse square of the design order, while achieving fixed-error discrimination requires a number of samples that grows as the square of the design order.
items.citation: Jian Yao, Quntao Zhuang. Hypothesis testing between quantum ensembles. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis
items.summary: This paper investigated how large language model agents perform root cause analysis for microservice failures, arguing that existing evaluations focused solely on whether the correct service is identified as the fault source, rather than examining the quality of the diagnostic reasoning process itself. The researchers developed a trajectory-level evaluation framework that assesses agent behavior against manually curated fault-propagation paths, analyzing thousands of diagnostic trajectories to characterize how agents investigate and use retrieved telemetry. They found a significant disconnect between endpoint correctness and diagnostic quality, where an agent can correctly identify the faulty service without properly reconstructing how the fault propagated through the system. The study identified failure modes including omission of decisive evidence, misinterpretation of retrieved evidence, and unsupported inference, and taxonomized these into a framework that informed a two-stage architecture called DiagGuard, which grounds observations before localization and audits the resulting diagnosis. DiagGuard demonstrated meaningful improvement in localization accuracy on an independent benchmark with a different model and service topology, showing that trajectory-level evaluation reveals limitations hidden by final-answer metrics and offers actionable paths for improving automated root cause analysis.
items.citation: Qisheng Lu, Aoyang Fang, Junjielong Xu et al.. Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, synthesizing evidence that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for tuberculosis detection and drug-resistance testing into a single framework. Digital chest radiography supported by computer-aided detection has been established as a core screening and triage tool, while decentralised molecular diagnosis has expanded through multiple platforms including low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests, novel specimen types such as tongue swabs, and innovations like sputum pooling to improve efficiency. Drug-resistance testing has advanced through rapid molecular tools and targeted next-generation sequencing, now endorsed for comprehensive susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays improve diagnostic yield in people with HIV and advanced disease but remain limited in broader application. Host blood transcriptomic and other biomarker signatures show promise for prognosis and triage, yet no biomarker has met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test that reliably distinguishes infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The authors conclude that substantial performance, implementation, and equity gaps persist, highlighting ongoing priorities for the field.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how the diagnosis of HIV-associated tuberculosis has evolved from 1990 to the present, focusing on the challenges posed by lower bacillary loads in sputum, high rates of extrapulmonary or disseminated disease, and the nonspecific clinical presentation in people with HIV. The authors trace the limitations of smear microscopy, which was the only rapid diagnostic tool available until 2011 and performs poorly in this population, contributing to both underdiagnosis and overdiagnosis with serious consequences for patient outcomes. The introduction of nucleic acid amplification tests and the urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assay, alongside antiretroviral therapy, has substantially changed the diagnostic landscape and contributed to reductions in tuberculosis incidence and mortality. However, the review concludes that current rapid diagnostic tests still fall short of ideal sensitivity, and only the urine lipoarabinomannan assay combines affordability with suitability for point-of-care use. The authors therefore argue that further development of accurate, affordable, and simple point-of-care diagnostics remains an urgent priority.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Operationalization of rapid molecular test coverage for tuberculosis in different international contexts: a scoping review.
items.summary: This scoping review examined how coverage of rapid molecular testing for tuberculosis has been operationalized and measured across different international settings. Following established scoping review guidelines, the authors searched multiple major databases for studies published over roughly a decade and a half, ultimately including studies that spanned a wide range of countries and contexts. The review found substantial conceptual heterogeneity in how coverage was defined, encompassing measures as varied as testing proportions within specific populations, equipment availability, and geographic accessibility, with no standardization across countries. Reported coverage values varied enormously, and socioeconomic, structural, financial, and facility-access challenges consistently emerged as barriers to test use. The authors conclude that achieving comparable monitoring of rapid molecular test coverage will require governmental commitment, decentralization of testing services, and adoption of uniform measurement criteria aligned with World Health Organization guidelines.
items.venue: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P
items.citation: Silva DHMD, Valença ABM, Ferreira MRL et al.. Operationalization of rapid molecular test coverage for tuberculosis in different international contexts: a scoping review.. Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P. 2026

items.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Urine-Based Molecular Testing for Urogenital Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of urine-based molecular testing methods — including Xpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis/rifampicin, multiplex polymerase chain reaction, and loop-mediated isothermal amplification — for detecting urogenital tuberculosis, a condition that is difficult to confirm rapidly using conventional culture. The authors pooled data from diagnostic accuracy studies involving patients with high clinical suspicion of urogenital tuberculosis, assessing sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratios using a bivariate random-effects model. Urine-based molecular testing demonstrated high specificity and a strong area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, though sensitivity was more modest, indicating the tests are better at ruling in than ruling out the disease. The choice of reference standard influenced specificity estimates, with culture-based references yielding perfect specificity compared to composite reference standards. The authors conclude that urine-based molecular testing offers high diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility as an adjunctive tool for rapid confirmation of urogenital tuberculosis, particularly when combined with clinical, imaging, and culture findings.
items.citation: Fang L, Chen X, Chen J et al.. Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Urine-Based Molecular Testing for Urogenital Tuberculosis.. Archivos espanoles de urologia. 2026

items.title: Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.
items.summary: This review examines blood-based diagnostic approaches for tuberculosis, focusing on serological methods as alternatives to conventional sputum culture and molecular assays. The authors survey the landscape of novel biomarkers being identified for TB serodiagnosis, with particular emphasis on their utility for detecting extrapulmonary tuberculosis and in patients who yield negative results from standard diagnostic tools. The review also considers how advanced diagnostic technologies can be integrated with these biomarkers to enhance performance. The authors argue that serological diagnosis offers practical advantages in simplicity, speed, and cost-effectiveness, making it especially relevant for diverse clinical settings where conventional diagnostics fall short.
items.citation: Yue C, Geng X, Sun X et al.. Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.. Clinical chemistry and laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study compared two WHO-endorsed nucleic acid amplification tests, Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, for diagnosing pulmonary tuberculosis and detecting rifampicin resistance in presumptive pulmonary tuberculosis patients in India. Using mycobacterial culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing as reference standards, the researchers prospectively enrolled patients at a tuberculosis centre in New Delhi and tested paired sputum specimens on both platforms while also recording operational and cost parameters. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra demonstrated higher sensitivity and specificity for tuberculosis detection as well as lower rates of invalid and indeterminate results compared to Truenat MTB Plus, though both platforms showed strong overall diagnostic performance. Truenat was considerably less expensive per test and holds advantages for decentralized deployment, but its substantially higher rates of invalid and indeterminate results increase the operational burden through the need for repeat testing. The authors conclude that a tiered diagnostic approach using each platform according to its strengths could help expand molecular testing access and advance tuberculosis elimination efforts.
items.citation: Sidiq Z, Anand A, Dwivedi KK et al.. Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Sepsis
items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years
items.summary: The paper reports on the implementation and early outcomes of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme, which uses low-dose computed tomography to detect lung cancer in high-risk individuals aged 55 to 74 who have ever smoked and meet risk thresholds determined by multivariable models. The programme, launched in 2019 and structured through regionally federated clinical infrastructure with national strategic and economic frameworks, has scaled rapidly across England with full national coverage expected by the end of the decade. Over five years, more than two million people were invited, resulting in thousands of lung cancer diagnoses, the majority of which were detected at early tumor stages, representing a shift toward earlier-stage diagnosis compared with historical patterns, particularly in socioeconomically deprived regions. The programme demonstrates that large-scale lung cancer screening can be implemented rapidly and feasibly through centralized protocols and effective project management, reaching high-risk and underserved populations. However, the authors note that inequalities in participation remain a challenge, and they propose that the programme's findings and tools support broader adoption of lung cancer screening across the UK and internationally.
items.citation: Richard W. Lee, Arjun Nair, Haval Balata et al.. Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities
items.summary: This review examines the NLRP3 inflammasome, a key signaling platform of the innate immune system capable of detecting a wide range of microbial, metabolic, and environmental danger signals. Upon activation, the complex recruits ASC and caspase-1 to drive maturation of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 and to execute pyroptotic cell death. The authors provide a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying NLRP3 activation, including ion flux, mitochondrial damage, lysosomal rupture, reactive oxygen species, and post-translational modifications, as well as the negative regulatory pathways that maintain inflammasome homeostasis. Aberrant NLRP3 activity is linked to a broad spectrum of diseases, spanning autoinflammatory syndromes, metabolic and cardiovascular conditions, neurodegeneration, and cancer. The review concludes by surveying emerging therapeutic strategies—including direct inhibitors, allosteric modulators, biologics, and repurposed drugs—that target the inflammasome and may offer translational potential across inflammatory and immune-related diseases.
items.citation: Chan Zou, Shilong Jiang, Hui Li et al.. The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review paper examines the molecular mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disorder characterized by pain, inflammation, and bone deterioration, with a focus on identifying new therapeutic targets. The authors analyze nociceptive pathways connecting the knee joint to the central nervous system, pathological changes in bone and cartilage, and the contributions of inflammatory cytokines to disease progression. A central focus is placed on organelle-level dysfunctions, specifically mitochondrial impairment with excessive reactive oxygen species production, lysosomal destabilization driven by hydroxyapatite digestion, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress resulting from compensatory protein overproduction, all of which collectively drive cartilage degradation. Building on these mechanistic insights, the review outlines emerging pharmacological strategies that simultaneously target inflammatory cascades, restore organelle homeostasis through approaches such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and attenuate pain signaling. The authors further highlight organelle-targeted drug delivery systems as a means to improve therapeutic efficacy, proposing a multimodal treatment framework aimed at addressing both the structural and clinical manifestations of osteoarthritis.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: AI-induced never-skilling in medical education
items.citation: Yuhe Ke, Liyuan Jin, Jasmine Chiat Ling Ong et al.. AI-induced never-skilling in medical education. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: EULAR recommendations for the management of Behçet’s syndrome: 2025 update
items.summary: This paper presents the updated clinical practice recommendations from a major European rheumatology alliance for managing Behçet's syndrome, a complex multisystem inflammatory disorder. A large multidisciplinary international task force used a structured process involving Delphi surveys, systematic literature review, and expert voting to revise and develop guidance statements. The update produced five overarching principles and twelve recommendations organized by organ involvement, of which one was entirely new and most of the remainder were modified from the previous version. Key treatment guidance emphasizes colchicine as first-line therapy for mucocutaneous and joint manifestations, with apremilast and TNFα inhibitors reserved for refractory cases, while more severe organ-threatening disease warrants early aggressive use of glucocorticoids, immunosuppressives, and monoclonal TNFα inhibitors. The overarching principles stress individualized treatment based on disease activity and prognostic factors, a multidisciplinary approach, patient education, and shared decision-making to optimize care quality.
items.citation: Gulen Hatemi, Sofia Ramiro, Yeşim Özgüler et al.. EULAR recommendations for the management of Behçet’s syndrome: 2025 update. Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. 2026

items.title: Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of unreliable agent execution of natural-language workflows, which suffer from implicit data dependencies and agent failures under complex or lengthy instructions. The authors developed Artic, a compiler that transforms natural-language workflows into artifact-driven representations where each step explicitly declares the data it reads and writes, with constraints on produced artifacts and explicit control flow transfers. The compiler identifies steps that impose excessive state dependencies or complex control logic and refines them through constrained optimization, while validating the transformation through decomposed faithfulness checks and scenario-based dry runs. Evaluated on a large set of problem instances drawn from diverse real-world domain workflows, Artic substantially improved task resolution rates compared to uncompiled text workflows. The system also demonstrated considerably greater consistency when the compiled workflows were executed across different language models and across repeated runs of the same model.
items.citation: Xiangzhe Xu, Hanxi Guo, Guangyu Shen et al.. Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation
items.summary: This paper introduces Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), a framework that encodes anatomical knowledge into deep learning models either as soft penalty terms in the loss function or as hard constraints built directly into the network architecture, drawing explicit analogy to physics-informed neural networks. The approach is developed around the clinical problem of how the aortoiliac arterial tree deforms when a stiff guidewire is inserted endoluminally, which is relevant to aortic surgery and autonomous endovascular navigation. Vessel centerlines and wire paths are lifted from ordinary three-dimensional space into curves of frames within the Lie group SE(3), coupling a Cosserat-rod wire model to an anatomically anchored vessel through a contact inequality constraint, with the deformation found as a constrained minimizer of coupled elastic energy. A Wasserstein-2 optimal-transport loss between predicted angiographic projections and observed two-dimensional angiograms allows three-dimensional deformation predictions to be trained from two-dimensional imaging data. The work currently presents and verifies the mathematical and mechanical framework rather than training a network, with future work planned to apply the model to real CT data and assess whether the anatomical priors improve accuracy and reduce data requirements.
items.citation: David P. Stonko. Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: This paper examines the deployment of autonomous AI diagnostic agents across eHealth platforms in sub-Saharan Africa, where these systems analyze patient clinical data and produce diagnostic or triage outputs without mandatory real-time human review. The authors argue that existing accountability, transparency, and explainability frameworks are predominantly clinician-centered and presuppose regulatory conditions that do not exist in low-resource settings, leaving a structural accountability gap rooted in patient unawareness of AI involvement in their care. Drawing on documented deployment cases involving tuberculosis detection, diabetic retinopathy screening, and mobile chatbot triage in Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana respectively, the paper demonstrates that these governance deficiencies are already manifest in active real-world systems. In response, the authors synthesize literature on informed consent, algorithmic accountability, and explainable AI to propose three foundational principles: agent-aware informed consent, human override as a structural requirement, and contextually adapted explainability. These principles are presented as a practical minimum standard for developers, health administrators, and policymakers operating in contexts where formal AI regulation remains nascent.
items.citation: Percy Brown, Kweku Yamoah. Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) in a timely manner, noting that conventional machine learning approaches relying on clinical and laboratory data introduce problematic delays. To overcome this limitation, the authors focused on home monitoring scenarios using only respiratory data collected from daily-use ventilators, which provides a more continuous and immediate data stream. They developed a Time-Aware transformer-based model designed to capture both the symptomatic patterns and their temporal progression within ventilator data, generating meaningful patient representations. Experimental results showed that this approach outperformed traditional methods across multiple classification tasks, suggesting it could meaningfully improve the speed and accuracy of AECOPD prediction in real-world home settings.
items.citation: Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Dongyang Wang et al.. Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hypothesis testing between quantum ensembles
items.summary: This paper studies the problem of distinguishing between two quantum state ensembles through binary hypothesis testing, addressing the fact that ensembles carry operational information beyond their average density operators due to the classical labels accompanying sampled states. The authors formulate a general framework for this discrimination task by analyzing the joint sampled state conditioned on an observed label pattern, which they show can be characterized by power-weighted ensemble moments. From this, they derive the Bayes-optimal measurement and exact finite-sample error probabilities, demonstrating that discrimination depends on the full moment hierarchy up to the number of samples taken. In the many-sample regime, they establish Chernoff bounds and exact error exponents for finite uniform pure-state ensembles, with applications to optical communication and quantum designs. For pure-state designs with large design order, they find that the maximal discrimination exponent decreases sharply with the design order, while achieving fixed error requires a number of samples that grows quadratically with the design order.
items.citation: Jian Yao, Quntao Zhuang. Hypothesis testing between quantum ensembles. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis
items.summary: This paper examined how large language model agents perform root cause analysis for microservice failures, arguing that existing evaluations which only check whether the correct service is identified are insufficient for understanding diagnostic quality. The researchers developed a trajectory-level evaluation framework that assesses agent reasoning processes against manually curated fault-propagation paths, analyzing thousands of diagnostic trajectories to characterize investigative behavior and telemetry use. They found a systematic disconnect between answer correctness and diagnostic quality, where agents could correctly identify a faulty service without reconstructing how the fault propagated, and identified recurring failure modes including omitted evidence, misinterpretation of retrieved telemetry, and unsupported inference. Based on this taxonomy, they developed DiagGuard, a two-stage architecture that grounds the diagnosis in available observations before localization and then audits the result, improving top-one accuracy in an independent evaluation setting. The work demonstrates that final-answer metrics conceal meaningful limitations in automated root cause analysis and that trajectory-level evaluation yields actionable improvements to agent design.
items.citation: Qisheng Lu, Aoyang Fang, Junjielong Xu et al.. Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending a non-governmental organisation-led clinic near Beirut, Lebanon, while also assessing their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Using a cross-sectional design over four months, researchers conducted sexual health consultations, administered STI and HIV tests, and collected anonymous questionnaire data covering demographics, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived HIV-related stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated, Lebanese men who identified as MSM, with a notable proportion living with HIV. Despite high levels of STI and HIV awareness among participants, condomless sex and recreational drug use were common, and perceived stigma and community beliefs emerged as significant barriers to testing. The findings suggest that integrating point-of-care testing into sexual health services enables same-day counselling and rapid linkage to confirmatory testing and care, while underscoring the need to address HIV-related stigma to reduce risky behaviours in this population.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.
items.summary: This study examined the economic costs of integrating point-of-care screening for three curable sexually transmitted infections into antenatal care in Zimbabwe, compared to syndromic management as a standard of care comparator. Researchers implemented testing at two primary healthcare clinics in Harare and collected economic cost data through staff interviews, time-and-motion studies, and review of study records, then modelled implementation in a low-volume routine care setting over a twelve-month period. The composite prevalence of the three infections was substantial among pregnant women screened, and the largest cost drivers were test kits and personnel, which together accounted for the majority of total intervention costs. The incremental cost per person screened and per person treated using point-of-care testing exceeded that of syndromic management, with test kit costs being the dominant factor. The authors conclude that reductions in the cost of point-of-care diagnostics will be essential for making such antenatal screening strategies more economically viable.
items.citation: Martin K, Bath D, Nyamwanza R et al.. Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections is cost-effective in remote Australian primary care settings serving First Nations communities, where the burden of chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and trichomonas is particularly high among young people. Using a decision analytic model with a government payer perspective over a ten-year time horizon, researchers compared costs and health outcomes of point-of-care testing against standard laboratory-based testing for individuals aged sixteen to twenty-nine years seeking care. The model found that the point-of-care programme was cost-effective relative to a commonly used willingness-to-pay threshold, with the result most sensitive to the probability of infection and the likelihood of receiving treatment within two days. The programme was also predicted to substantially reduce rates of pelvic inflammatory disease and preterm or low birth weight births among those with an infection. The authors conclude that sustained implementation of this scaled point-of-care testing approach is likely to be cost-effective and to improve reproductive health outcomes in remote primary care settings.
items.citation: Watts CG, Causer LM, Matthews SJ et al.. Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.
items.summary: This review examines the epidemiology, pathogenic mechanisms, diagnosis, and prevention of anorectal bacterial sexually transmitted infections, focusing primarily on chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and syphilis, whose global incidence continues to rise despite available testing. The authors explore why these infections are frequently asymptomatic, particularly among men who have sex with men, attributing this to bacterial adaptation to rectal tissues and attenuated local immune responses. Molecular diagnostics have substantially improved detection, though challenges remain in distinguishing viable from non-viable organisms, expanding point-of-care testing, and reconciling broad screening with antimicrobial stewardship goals. Treatment strategies are evolving in response to emerging antimicrobial resistance, especially for gonorrhoea, while prevention advances such as doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis show meaningful reductions in chlamydia and syphilis incidence alongside emerging applications of artificial intelligence. The review identifies key knowledge gaps and proposes research priorities to improve control of these infections across diverse clinical settings.
items.citation: Latt PM, Kong FYS, Khosropour CM et al.. Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.. Nature reviews. Gastroenterology & hepatology. 2026

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Testing and Screening Strategies for Trichomoniasis among Asymptomatic and Symptomatic Women in U.S. Outpatient Clinical Settings.
items.summary: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of various testing and screening strategies for *Trichomonas vaginalis* among both symptomatic and asymptomatic women in U.S. primary care settings. Using a decision tree model applied to a hypothetical cohort of women aged 15–59, the researchers assessed combinations of wet mount microscopy, rapid antigen testing, and nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT), estimating health outcomes in quality-adjusted life years and costs associated with trichomonas-related sequelae over the cohort's lifetime. They found that adding NAAT to wet mount microscopy for symptomatic women improved health outcomes and fell within a commonly accepted cost-effectiveness threshold, making it the most economically justifiable approach. By contrast, adding NAAT to rapid antigen testing for symptomatic women and universal NAAT screening of asymptomatic women both exceeded that threshold and were not considered cost-effective. The findings suggest that while enhanced testing in symptomatic women can be economically warranted, broader population screening strategies would require substantially higher willingness-to-pay thresholds to be justified.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Rong R, Stoecker C, Kissinger PJ et al.. Cost-Effectiveness of Testing and Screening Strategies for Trichomoniasis among Asymptomatic and Symptomatic Women in U.S. Outpatient Clinical Settings.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions
