items.summary: This narrative review examines the current state of scientific knowledge on Compulsive Sexual Behavior Disorder and Problematic Pornography Use, two constructs that remain contested in terms of their nature, classification, and clinical significance. Drawing on contributions from experts across psychology, psychiatry, sexology, addiction science, and neuroscience, the authors synthesized empirical and theoretical literature spanning eleven key thematic areas, including conceptualization, assessment, epidemiology, etiology, co-occurring disorders, consequences, and treatment. The review also addressed underrepresented groups such as adolescents, women, and LGBTQ+ individuals, as well as the role of cultural factors in shaping how these behaviors are understood and experienced. The authors identify persistent methodological challenges and ongoing controversies in the field, highlighting that debates over classification and measurement continue to limit scientific progress. The work calls for greater interdisciplinary collaboration and more rigorous research designs to advance both clinical practice and public health responses to dysregulated sexual behavior.
items.citation: Campbell Ince, Stephanie Antons, Sarah Ashton et al.. Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions. Journal of Behavioral Addictions. 2026

items.title: Technological effects on gender studies: An intersectional perspective
items.summary: This paper examined how digitalization and technologization interact with gender dynamics, exploring whether digital transformation constitutes a fundamental shift in how gender identities are constructed, performed, and contested. The researchers conducted a systematic literature review of recent high-impact scholarship, drawing on perspectives from sociology, feminist theory, communication studies, health informatics, and STEM education. The analysis found that while digital technologies offer emancipatory possibilities through anonymity, accessibility, and broader public participation, they simultaneously replicate and intensify patriarchal structures via cyberviolence, algorithmic bias, digital exclusion, and the persistent underrepresentation of women in STEM. The paper concludes that digital spaces are not ideologically neutral but function as contested terrains where existing power relations are renegotiated in new forms, and that geographic and disciplinary gaps remain in how these issues are studied. The authors call for intersectional, gender-sensitive policies and multi-stakeholder collaborations to resist the reproduction of masculine dominance and to build more equitable technological ecosystems.
items.venue: Feminist Encounters A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics
items.citation: Şevki Işıklı, Esra Fatma FAZLIOĞLU. Technological effects on gender studies: An intersectional perspective. Feminist Encounters A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics. 2026

items.title: An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening
items.summary: This thesis examined epidemiological methods for controlling sexually transmitted diseases, with particular focus on identifying asymptomatic individuals through contact tracing and screening. The research evaluated contact tracing procedures for gonorrhoea and HIV, screened asymptomatic women at family planning clinics for chlamydia, compared chlamydial infection characteristics across different patient groups, and investigated whether contact tracing data could inform models of partner choice and disease spread. Contact tracing proved effective in controlling a gonorrhoea outbreak and identified previously unknown HIV-positive individuals, while chlamydia screening revealed meaningful prevalence among asymptomatic attendees and identified key risk factors including young age, short relationship duration, and lack of condom use. Comparing chlamydia index cases found through screening versus those attending specialist clinics showed only small differences in partner numbers and infection rates, leading to the conclusion that different management approaches for the two groups are not justified. Data on partner selection indicated that steady partner choice was relatively restricted while casual partner choice was more random, which does not support a purely random mixing model for modelling sexually transmitted disease spread.
items.citation: Kristina Ramstedt. An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening. Acta Dermato Venereologica. 2026

items.title: Multifactorial determinants of health status: insights from the MEDIET4ALL large-scale survey on eco-sociodemographic, psychological, and lifestyle (diet, physical activity, and sleep) factors
items.summary: This large-scale survey study investigated the multifactorial determinants of individual health status, encompassing geo-demographic, socioeconomic, psychological, and lifestyle variables, among participants from Mediterranean and neighboring countries. Using multinomial logistic regression and related statistical approaches applied to data from the MEDIET4ALL e-survey, researchers categorized participants as healthy, at-risk, or having diagnosed diseases and identified factors associated with each category. Body mass index emerged as the strongest negative predictor of health status, with both obesity and underweight substantially increasing the odds of being at-risk or having disease, while psychological distress, insomnia, alcohol consumption, and prolonged sitting time were also significant negative predictors. Conversely, life satisfaction was the strongest protective factor, followed by higher education, better sleep quality, and adherence to the Mediterranean diet and lifestyle, with socioeconomic variables such as employment status and rural living environment also conferring protection. The authors conclude that health outcomes reflect a complex interplay of lifestyle, mental health, and socio-environmental factors, underscoring the need for multi-level public health interventions and future longitudinal research to establish causal pathways.
items.citation: Achraf Ammar, Atef Salem, Mohamed Ali Boujelbane et al.. Multifactorial determinants of health status: insights from the MEDIET4ALL large-scale survey on eco-sociodemographic, psychological, and lifestyle (diet, physical activity, and sleep) factors. Frontiers in Public Health. 2026

items.title: A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks
items.summary: This study examined the relationship between housing instability and drug overdose risk among young people who inject drugs, arguing that existing research has been limited by treating housing instability as a single-dimensional construct. Using baseline data from a network-based longitudinal study of young people who inject drugs and their social networks in metropolitan Chicago, the researchers developed a multi-dimensional housing instability risk index composed of five dichotomous variables and analyzed its association with lifetime overdose count using negative binomial regression. After adjusting for multiple covariates, they found a significant positive association between the composite housing instability risk score and lifetime number of overdoses. The findings support the value of a multi-dimensional approach to measuring housing instability, suggesting that interventions aimed at reducing overdose risk should address the complexity of housing precarity in a more holistic manner.
items.citation: Kathleen Kristensen, Leslie D. Williams, Charlie Kaplan et al.. A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks. Journal of Urban Health. 2026

items.title: Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads
items.summary: This paper studied the development of an enzyme-free platform for ultrasensitive protein detection aimed at improving accessibility in resource-limited settings and low- and middle-income countries. The researchers created a digital protein detection assay called efMOSAIC that uses hybridization chain reaction-based signal amplifiers instead of enzymes, combined with magnetic beads, to quantify protein biomarkers. The platform achieves detection limits comparable to established single-molecule detection methods such as Simoa, representing a sensitivity far beyond conventional ELISA assays. Critically, the signal amplifier reagents remained stable when stored at room temperature for at least six months, eliminating the need for cold chain infrastructure. The platform was validated for detecting cytokines from human plasma and demonstrated multiplexed biomarker capability, suggesting it could enable ultrasensitive diagnostics outside of centralized laboratory settings.
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.citation: Karan Malhotra, Louise L. Hansen, Samuel Han et al.. Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads. Journal of the American Chemical Society. 2026

items.title: Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution
items.summary: This paper investigates the reliability gap between natural-language workflows and their actual execution by AI agents, identifying that implicit data dependencies and complex control logic cause agents to fail when following such instructions. The authors developed Artic, a compiler that transforms natural-language workflows into structured, artifact-driven representations where each step explicitly declares what data it reads and writes, with constraints on outputs and explicit control flow transfers. The compiler also identifies steps that place excessive demands on agent execution and refines them through constrained optimization, while validating the transformation through decomposed faithfulness checks and scenario-based dry runs. Evaluating across hundreds of problem instances drawn from real-world domain workflows, the approach substantially improves task resolution rates compared to using the original text workflows. The compiled workflows also demonstrate markedly greater consistency when executed across different language models and across repeated runs of the same model.
items.citation: Xiangzhe Xu, Hanxi Guo, Guangyu Shen et al.. Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation
items.summary: This paper introduces Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), a framework that encodes anatomical knowledge into deep learning models either as soft penalty terms in the loss function or as hard constraints built directly into the network architecture, analogous to how physics-informed neural networks incorporate physical laws. The approach is developed around a clinical problem with limited data availability: predicting how the aortoiliac vasculature deforms when a stiff guidewire is inserted during endovascular procedures, which is relevant to aortic surgery and autonomous endovascular navigation. The vessel centerline and wire path are represented as curves of frames in the Lie group SE(3), and a Cosserat-rod mechanical model of the wire is coupled to the vessel through a contact inequality constraint, with deformation predicted as a constrained minimizer of coupled elastic energy. Training supervision uses a Wasserstein-2 optimal-transport loss comparing predicted two-dimensional projections through imaging geometry against observed angiograms, enabling three-dimensional predictions to be learned from two-dimensional data. The current work establishes and verifies the kinematic, mechanical, and projection framework without yet training a network, with future work planned to transfer the model to real clinical data to improve predictive accuracy and reduce training data requirements.
items.citation: David P. Stonko. Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hypothesis testing between quantum ensembles
items.summary: This paper studies the problem of distinguishing between two quantum state ensembles, which are collections of quantum states paired with classical labels and invariant under label permutations. The authors develop a formal framework for binary hypothesis testing between finite quantum ensembles, deriving the Bayes-optimal measurement strategy and exact finite-sample error probabilities by expressing the joint sampled state in terms of power-weighted ensemble moments. They show that the ability to discriminate between ensembles depends on the full hierarchy of ensemble moments up to the number of samples observed, rather than just the average density operators. In the asymptotic regime, they derive Chernoff-type bounds and exact error exponents for finite uniform pure-state ensembles. Applying their framework to optical communication and quantum designs, they find that for pure-state designs with large design order, the optimal discrimination exponent decreases sharply with design order while the sample complexity required for reliable discrimination grows correspondingly.
items.citation: Jian Yao, Quntao Zhuang. Hypothesis testing between quantum ensembles. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental tension in Test-Time Training (TTT) approaches to long-context sequence modeling, where per-token weight updates during inference are expressive but computationally expensive, while chunk-wise approximations are efficient but sacrifice important temporal structure. The authors propose a method called E²-TTT that derives a closed-form state transition under standard chunk approximations, allowing it to exactly reproduce the fast-weight and momentum states of per-token recurrence at chunk boundaries while enabling full parallelization. By preserving the temporal dynamics of the update rule that prior chunk-wise methods discard, the approach reconciles expressivity with hardware efficiency without sacrificing training throughput. When trained on models up to a substantial parameter count from scratch, E²-TTT matches or exceeds previous TTT and hybrid attention baselines on language modeling and in-context retrieval tasks. Its most striking advantage appears in length extrapolation, retaining strong passkey retrieval accuracy far beyond its training context length while achieving competitive training throughput.
items.citation: Zeyun Zhong, Joya Chen, Manuel Martin et al.. Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Basin-Preserving Discretizations of Modern Hopfield Retrieval Dynamics: Energy Cells, Dissipation, and the Attention Limit
items.summary: This paper studies the retrieval dynamics of modern Hopfield networks, which are governed by a log-sum-exp energy whose gradient flow describes continuous-time memory retrieval, while the attention update corresponds to an exact discrete minimization step. The central question is which time discretizations preserve not just energy decay and fixed points, but the full basins of attraction—the regions of state space from which each memory pattern is reliably recovered. The authors introduce the concept of "energy cells," defined as connected components of sublevel sets containing exactly one attractor and no other critical point, and prove that every finite energy cell below a critical escape energy is simultaneously preserved by the continuous flow, relaxed attention maps over a broad parameter range, and implicit Euler integration within its uniqueness regime. Additional results include local contraction bounds near well-separated patterns with a certified optimal overrelaxation, characterization of proximal tunneling and overshoot outside the preservation regimes, an order barrier for scalar reparametrizations, a second-order scalar-auxiliary-variable scheme, and extensions to damped difference-of-convex iterations in Bregman geometry. Numerical experiments across nine campaigns validate the theoretical bounds and confirm that observed disagreements between continuous and discrete retrieval occur only above the attractor-specific escape energy level.
items.citation: Francisco R. Villatoro. Basin-Preserving Discretizations of Modern Hopfield Retrieval Dynamics: Energy Cells, Dissipation, and the Attention Limit. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fault Diagnosis of Dynamic Systems Under Unknown Operating Conditions: A Condition-Guided Selective Adaptation Approach
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of diagnosing faults in dynamic industrial systems when operating conditions are unknown and shifting, which typically causes conventional diagnostic models to degrade in performance. The proposed approach combines an offline training phase, in which a continuous operating-condition adversarial learning strategy with progressive training is used to build a more generalizable diagnostic model, with an online deployment phase that leverages residual operating-condition responses to identify reliable unlabeled samples from streaming data for continual model updating. This two-stage condition-guided selective adaptation framework is evaluated on real-world gearbox and motor datasets, where it is shown to outperform existing state-of-the-art methods in diagnostic accuracy while keeping test-time computationally manageable, suggesting practical viability for industrial deployment.
items.citation: Jiaming Liu, Zeyi Liu, Hongshuo Zhao et al.. Fault Diagnosis of Dynamic Systems Under Unknown Operating Conditions: A Condition-Guided Selective Adaptation Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.
items.summary: The paper studied the detection of *Shigella flexneri 2a*, the predominant cause of shigellosis and a major public health burden in developing countries, using CRISPR-based diagnostic technology. The researchers developed a CRISPR-Cas12a assay that couples recombinase polymerase amplification with Cas12a-mediated collateral cleavage, targeting two serotype-specific genes unique to *S. flexneri 2a*, and validated it against a large cohort of clinical stool specimens. The assay achieved a detection limit comparable to conventional PCR, demonstrated complete analytical specificity with no cross-reactivity to other bacteria, and completed the isothermal reaction within one hour at room temperature without specialized equipment. Clinical validation showed high diagnostic sensitivity and specificity, comparable to PCR performance on the same specimens, with results readable via either fluorescence or lateral flow. The authors conclude that the assay's speed, simplicity, and accuracy make it well-suited for point-of-care diagnostics and field-based surveillance in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Liao J, Su Y, Jiang F. CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated an integrated centrifugal microfluidic diagnostic platform called iCARD for rapid multiplexed detection of respiratory pathogens at the point of care. The system combines a polymethyl methacrylate disc pre-loaded with lyophilized CRISPR/Cas13a reagents, centrifugal microfluidics, and a portable fluorescence analyzer, along with a novel resin-based nucleic acid purification method for throat swab samples. The platform enables automated parallel screening of six respiratory pathogens across four independent samples in a single run. Analytical validation demonstrated single-copy sensitivity with no cross-reactivity, and clinical testing using retrospective patient throat swabs showed high diagnostic sensitivity and perfect specificity. The authors conclude that iCARD is a robust, high-throughput tool suited for decentralized molecular screening and epidemiological surveillance.
items.citation: Li L, Wei H, Wei M et al.. An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: CRISPR RNA Engineering Enables Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Discrimination in Nucleic Acid Detection.
items.summary: This review examines how CRISPR-based diagnostic systems can be engineered to achieve single nucleotide polymorphism discrimination in nucleic acid detection, addressing a central limitation of current platforms—namely off-target activation and poor differentiation of closely related sequences. The authors synthesize advances in CRISPR RNA engineering strategies, detailing how structural features such as spacer length, intentional mismatch design, secondary-structure modulation, chemical modification, and strand-displacement gating collectively govern target recognition and cleavage fidelity. Computational prediction, high-throughput screening, and hybrid guide architectures are examined for their roles in elevating specificity, stabilizing assay performance, and enabling multiplexed detection for pathogen profiling and mutation identification. The review also identifies persistent challenges including interference from complex clinical samples, absence of unified evaluation standards, and scalability barriers that impede translation to clinical settings. The authors conclude that integrating refined crRNA design with system-level optimization and standardized benchmarking will be critical to realizing ultrasensitive, portable point-of-care diagnostics capable of supporting precision medicine and infectious disease surveillance.
items.citation: Sun T, Yuan A, Xie W et al.. CRISPR RNA Engineering Enables Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Discrimination in Nucleic Acid Detection.. Angewandte Chemie (International ed. in English). 2026

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of point-of-care testing technologies developed for SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis, motivated by the urgent diagnostic demands exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases and evaluated multiple testing modalities, including molecular assays such as rapid RT-PCR, LAMP, and CRISPR-based methods, alongside antigen and antibody tests, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular methods were found to offer high sensitivity and specificity suitable for decentralized use, while antigen tests provide rapid and affordable screening though with variable performance depending on viral load and circulating variants. Antibody-based assays were deemed more appropriate for seroprevalence and retrospective purposes than for detecting acute infection, and emerging biosensor and AI systems showed promise but largely remain at prototype stages requiring further clinical validation. The review concludes that no single modality is universally optimal, and that complementary use of these approaches, alongside advances in multiplexing, digital connectivity, and variant-resilient detection, will be essential for both COVID-19 management and broader infectious disease preparedness.
items.citation: Hetta HF, Ahmed R, Haseeb A et al.. SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.
items.summary: This review examines a decade of progress in applying CRISPR-Cas systems to infectious disease management across three domains: diagnostics, therapeutic genome editing, and vaccine development. The authors surveyed translational advances in key platforms such as DETECTR and SHERLOCK for rapid pathogen detection, CRISPR-Cas9 strategies targeting viral genomes and antimicrobial resistance, and the engineering of live-attenuated and personalized neoantigen vaccines. Their analysis finds that CRISPR-based diagnostics have advanced furthest toward clinical evaluation, while therapeutic applications and personalized neoantigen vaccines remain at earlier, more exploratory stages, largely due to challenges in delivery and safety. The review uniquely integrates all three application areas within a single infectious disease framework and critically assesses technical, regulatory, and ethical barriers to clinical translation. The authors conclude that realizing the transformative potential of CRISPR-Cas in infectious disease will require overcoming obstacles related to delivery efficiency, off-target effects, and equitable regulatory oversight.
items.citation: Mayuri K, Saravanan KM, Somala CS et al.. CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.. Biochemical genetics. 2026

items.title: PCR and molecular diagnostics: Biotechnologic integration in clinical laboratories.
items.summary: This review paper examines the evolution and clinical integration of polymerase chain reaction technology and related molecular diagnostic tools in laboratory medicine. The authors survey the development of PCR from traditional amplification methods to advanced platforms including quantitative, digital, reverse-transcription, and multiplex variants, assessing how each contributes to nucleic acid detection, quantification, and high-throughput analysis. The paper also explores how PCR-based approaches can be combined with next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, microarrays, and epigenetic profiling to provide broader insight into disease states, with particular emphasis on clinically relevant cancer biomarkers used for early diagnosis, prognosis, treatment monitoring, and precision medicine. Applications in infectious disease diagnosis, antimicrobial resistance tracking, heritable disorder detection, and minimal residual disease monitoring are also discussed, alongside emerging trends in multi-omics data integration using artificial intelligence, liquid biopsy technologies, and point-of-care platforms. The authors acknowledge persistent challenges including costs, standardization, specialized expertise, and data management, while asserting that ongoing advances are progressively expanding access to these technologies for clinicians and patients.
items.venue: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
items.citation: Saleem MA, Riaz T, Saleem F et al.. PCR and molecular diagnostics: Biotechnologic integration in clinical laboratories.. Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, emphasizing how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity and specificity in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, enabling real-time analytics, pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection tools into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI. Looking forward, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-based traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: New approach methodologies for drug discovery
items.summary: This review examines the emergence and current state of new approach methodologies as alternatives to traditional animal-based drug discovery, which has historically suffered from high failure rates. The authors survey recent advances in stem cell-, organoid-, and computational approaches that now cover the full drug-discovery continuum, from disease modeling and drug design through efficacy testing. The review highlights progress in identifying therapeutic candidates and developing innovative models, and also considers the potential for these methodologies themselves to serve as treatments in preclinical and clinical settings. Key biological, technical, and regulatory obstacles limiting broad translational adoption are assessed alongside the evolving oversight frameworks from major regulatory and funding bodies. The authors conclude by outlining future human-centric pipelines and the translational and societal considerations necessary for responsible implementation of these approaches.
items.citation: Wenqiang Liu, Paul Pang, Catherine A. Wu et al.. New approach methodologies for drug discovery. Cell. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, focusing on how light-activated nanoparticles can be engineered to treat a broad spectrum of diseases with greater precision than conventional approaches. The authors survey core components and delivery platforms—including gold nanoparticles, liposomes, and dendrimers—that enhance light absorption, improve tissue targeting, and amplify therapeutic effects such as reactive oxygen species generation in photodynamic therapy and localized heating in photothermal therapy. At the molecular level, the review dissects how light-triggered interventions induce oxidative stress, activate apoptotic and autophagic pathways, and reshape immune responses through cytokine modulation and T-cell activity, with relevance not only to cancer but also to cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune conditions. The authors critically evaluate regulatory approvals and recent clinical trial data, identifying key barriers to broader clinical translation including nanoparticle optimization, effective light delivery to target tissues, and regulatory complexity. The review concludes that integrating molecular understanding with clinical experience positions nanoparticle-based phototherapy as a transformative noninvasive strategy with wide therapeutic potential.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Cell death in cancer
items.summary: This review examines the diverse programs of cell death relevant to cancer biology, framing the field around the well-established hallmark that cancer cells evade death to survive oncogenic stress and resist therapy. The authors synthesize knowledge spanning apoptosis and more recently characterized modalities including necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis, organizing these into a unified conceptual framework. A particular focus is placed on ferroptosis, which is driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and arises from metabolic perturbations rather than a canonical induction signal. The review highlights how non-apoptotic death programs can elicit inflammatory responses and shape interactions among tumor cells, stromal cells, and immune cells, thereby influencing the efficacy of immunotherapy. The authors also address mechanisms of resistance to cell death and immune suppression, positioning restoration of cell death as a promising therapeutic strategy in oncology.
items.citation: Marcus Conrad, Andreas Strasser, Philipp J. Jost et al.. Cell death in cancer. Cell. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infection with high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors comprehensively analyzed the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia alongside the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges that complicate its management. A central focus is placed on the limitations of conventional diagnostic methods that cause harmful delays, the growing problem of antifungal resistance, and the importance of susceptibility-guided therapy to improve patient outcomes. The review evaluates both established and emerging diagnostic technologies, as well as therapeutic strategies spanning empiric and targeted regimens, combination therapy, and novel antifungal agents currently in clinical development. Looking forward, the authors highlight promising future directions including artificial intelligence applications in diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches as potential tools to address the evolving complexity of candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development
items.summary: This narrative review examined the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance with a focus on the pathogens identified by the World Health Organization as priorities for research and drug development. The authors synthesized current understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which these bacteria resist antibiotics, including reduced membrane permeability, efflux pump overexpression, enzymatic inactivation, target modification, biofilm formation, and horizontal gene transfer. They critically assessed the shortcomings of conventional antibiotics and traditional discovery pipelines alongside the clinical and economic burden imposed by resistant infections. Emerging therapeutic strategies—such as artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, phage therapy, antimicrobial peptides, CRISPR-based approaches, and natural product-derived compounds—were evaluated for their pharmacological feasibility and translational challenges, including issues of toxicity, dosing, resistance emergence, and regulatory barriers. The review concludes that effectively addressing priority resistant pathogens will require integrated, multidisciplinary approaches that combine molecular biology, pharmacology, clinical translation, antimicrobial stewardship, surveillance, and a One Health framework spanning human, animal, and environmental health sectors.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Mahmoud M. Dahab et al.. The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Classical versus non-classical photon states for detecting vacuum non-linearity
items.summary: The paper investigates whether the detectability of quantum electrodynamic vacuum nonlinearity can be enhanced by injecting classical or non-classical photon states into optical modes that would otherwise be left in the vacuum state. Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum itself acts as a nonlinear medium, and experimental schemes designed to verify this prediction typically look for signal photons appearing in initially empty modes. The authors analyze what happens when those modes are instead seeded with classical or squeezed photon states before the interaction. They find that this modification can substantially improve the detectability of the vacuum nonlinearity signal compared to the standard vacuum-seeded approach.
items.citation: N. Ahmadiniaz, C. Kohlfürst, R. Shaisultanov et al.. Classical versus non-classical photon states for detecting vacuum non-linearity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Mining beyond Earth with Space Robots: Exploration, Sampling, and Extraction
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive review of robotic technologies for space mining, encompassing the exploration, sampling, and extraction of resources such as helium-3, water, minerals on the Moon and Mars, and asteroid deposits. The authors propose a systematic six-stage architecture that spans remote sensing for target identification, in situ robotic detection, single- and multi-robot sampling, autonomous extraction, and final integration into construction or transport operations. The review also surveys existing resources relevant to the field, including real-world mission data, terrestrial analog datasets, and simulation environments. The paper addresses the need for autonomous robotic systems given the challenges of harsh space conditions, communication delays, and high launch costs. The authors conclude by identifying open technological challenges and outlining a research roadmap aimed at advancing toward a sustainable off-world economy.
items.citation: Dong Li, Dujun Nie, Xiaotong Zhang et al.. Mining beyond Earth with Space Robots: Exploration, Sampling, and Extraction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ViTacPhys: Physical Property-Aware Grasping from Human Visual-Tactile Demonstrations
items.summary: This paper investigates whether explicitly estimating object physical properties from human demonstrations can improve robotic grasping policies. The authors developed ViTacPhys, a visual-tactile framework that estimates object mass, friction coefficient, and stiffness by combining temporal visual-tactile modeling, cross-attention multimodal fusion, and semantic priors from a vision-language model, trained on a dataset of rigid and deformable objects. The system achieves high classification accuracy and low stiffness estimation error on both seen and held-out objects. To deploy the system on a robot, the authors transferred the human-domain model using limited teleoperation data and augmentation strategies, then conditioned a grasping policy on the estimated physical properties. The resulting adaptive grasping policy achieved strong success rates on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution objects, with force profiles more closely matching human teleoperation behavior than a baseline method, demonstrating that explicit physical property estimation can meaningfully improve real-world robotic manipulation.
items.citation: Yiwen Liu, Yujun Zhu, Kui Jia et al.. ViTacPhys: Physical Property-Aware Grasping from Human Visual-Tactile Demonstrations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Magic Velocity Selection in Atom Interferometry
items.summary: The paper investigates a source of systematic error in atom interferometry arising from the use of velocity-selective Raman transitions to prepare atomic ensembles. Differential light shifts between atomic energy levels cause the selected velocity to depend on the local laser beam intensity, producing spatially correlated velocity distributions that interact with detuning-dependent systematic effects in a Bragg diffraction-based simultaneous conjugate Ramsey-Bordé interferometer. Through theoretical analysis, the authors show these interactions can induce systematic phase shifts at the level of tens of milliradians, which would be detrimental to precision measurements. They identify a "magic" detuning for the velocity-selection step at which this systematic phase shift is suppressed, because the spatial correlation between atom velocity and position is eliminated. Operating at this magic detuning is proposed as a practical technique for achieving sub-part-per-billion accuracy in high-resolution atom interferometry.
items.citation: Yuno Iwasaki, Jack Roth, Madeline Bernstein et al.. Magic Velocity Selection in Atom Interferometry. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Truthful Calibration Measures for Sequential Prediction
items.summary: This paper studies calibration measures for sequential probabilistic prediction, focusing on the tension between truthfulness (incentivizing honest probability reports), completeness (penalizing miscalibrated forecasters), and soundness (not penalizing well-calibrated ones). The authors first resolve an open question by proving that exact truthfulness is fundamentally incompatible with both completeness and soundness, even in the simple setting of independent binary outcomes. They then demonstrate that this impossibility is specific to the exact case by constructing two general reductions from any base calibration measure that yield additively and multiplicatively approximately truthful variants while preserving completeness and soundness. Applying the multiplicative reduction, they construct a family of sound and complete calibration measures with improved multiplicative truthfulness guarantees that strengthen prior work in the area.
items.citation: Anagha Gokul, Jason Hartline, Lunjia Hu et al.. Truthful Calibration Measures for Sequential Prediction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: TurboBias 2.0: Streaming Context-Biasing for Production-Efficient ASR Systems
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of incorporating user-specific context biasing into production automatic speech recognition systems while maintaining the strict latency and throughput requirements of real-world deployment. The authors developed TurboBias 2.0, a framework built on GPU-accelerated Transducer-based ASR that extends prior work with case-insensitive boosting graphs and per-stream batched decoding, allowing each utterance in a batch to carry its own independent context-biasing configuration. This design enables personalized phrase boosting for multiple simultaneous users without any mixing or sharing of their context lists, and supports both offline and streaming inference modes alongside greedy and beam-search decoding. Experiments demonstrate that the framework improves recognition accuracy for contextual phrases while preserving low latency and high throughput, making it suitable for practical production deployment.
items.citation: Vladimir Bataev, Lilit Grigoryan, Andrei Andrusenko et al.. TurboBias 2.0: Streaming Context-Biasing for Production-Efficient ASR Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ultrabright PCNs@Coumarin 6-Enhanced Wireless Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform for Ultrasensitive Detection of Porphyromonas gingivalis.
items.summary: This study developed an ultrasensitive wireless lateral flow immunoassay platform for detecting *Porphyromonas gingivalis*, a key bacterial pathogen linked to periodontal and systemic diseases, addressing the limitations of traditional detection methods such as low sensitivity and operational complexity. The platform integrated a novel fluorescent metal-organic framework nanocomposite with substantially enhanced fluorescence intensity and prolonged lifetime, combined with a quadruped DNA walker system that amplifies signal through DNAzyme activity. A self-developed wireless analyzer was incorporated to enable rapid and accurate interpretation of test strip results. The platform achieved an exceptionally low detection limit and a wide linear detection range, with validation on clinical saliva samples confirming high accuracy and strong resistance to interference at lower cost and greater convenience than polymerase chain reaction. The authors conclude that this platform is well-suited for point-of-care testing scenarios including chair-side diagnosis, home self-testing, and community-level screening.
items.citation: Zhou M, Shen H, Long Z et al.. Ultrabright PCNs@Coumarin 6-Enhanced Wireless Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform for Ultrasensitive Detection of Porphyromonas gingivalis.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a low-cost, noninvasive electronic nose could detect SARS-CoV-2 infection as an alternative to conventional diagnostic methods that are often uncomfortable and slow. The researchers developed a device using an array of commercially available metal-oxide gas sensors to analyze volatile organic compounds in both saliva and exhaled breath samples, which shift in chemical composition in response to viral infection. Multiple machine learning algorithms—including K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, Neural Networks, and Random Forest—were applied to classify infected versus non-infected samples from a real-world hospital cohort. Detection accuracy varied across algorithms and sample types, with exhaled breath performing slightly better than saliva, and the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm achieving the strongest discriminatory performance for both sample types. The authors conclude that this approach demonstrates proof-of-concept feasibility for point-of-care SARS-CoV-2 screening using an inexpensive and noninvasive sensor platform.
items.venue: The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases
items.citation: Fialkovitz G, Sousa PL, Hidifira AM et al.. Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.. The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that allow these devices to integrate seamlessly with the body over extended periods, as well as multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The integration of artificial intelligence for signal processing and predictive health insights is also discussed alongside the device architectures that enable these capabilities. The review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of AI-generated outputs. Overall, the paper synthesizes progress across materials science, sensor design, and AI-assisted strategies to outline the landscape of next-generation biosensing technologies.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Devices for Personalized Health Care Solutions: Systematic Review
items.summary: This systematic review examined the scope and impact of artificial intelligence integration in medical devices for personalized healthcare, analyzing how AI enables tailored treatments based on individual patient profiles including genetic data, medical history, and physiological parameters. The authors conducted a systematic review of peer-reviewed articles, industry analyses, and regulatory advisories published over roughly a seven-year period, assessing current applications, implementation barriers, and best practices across diagnostics, treatment personalization, wearable monitoring, and smart prosthetics. The review found substantial advances in AI-driven diagnostic accuracy and device functionality, while also identifying persistent challenges including data security risks, algorithmic bias, regulatory constraints, and difficulties integrating AI tools into existing healthcare infrastructures. Strategies such as improved data validation, clearer regulatory frameworks, and ethical guidelines were identified as effective in mitigating these obstacles, and emerging technologies including quantum computing and blockchain-based data management were highlighted as promising avenues for further improvement. The authors conclude that realizing the full potential of AI-driven personalized medicine requires coordinated effort across technical, ethical, and regulatory dimensions.
items.citation: Hemanth Ponnambalath Mohanadas, A Manikandan, Ahmad Fauzi Ismail et al.. Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Devices for Personalized Health Care Solutions: Systematic Review. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2026

items.title: Extracellular Vesicles: A Comprehensive Review of Their Origins, Functions, and Therapeutic Potential
items.summary: This review paper examines extracellular vesicles, with particular focus on the exosome subtype, covering their biological origins, functions, isolation methods, characterization techniques, and therapeutic applications. The authors describe how these membrane-bound particles arise from the endosomal pathway and serve as mediators of intercellular communication by transporting diverse molecular cargo including proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and metabolites. The paper surveys the landscape of isolation approaches such as ultracentrifugation, size-exclusion chromatography, and immunoaffinity capture, alongside characterization methods including nanoparticle tracking analysis, electron microscopy variants, and flow cytometry, noting the distinct trade-offs each method presents in purity, scalability, and vesicle integrity. The authors highlight the clinical promise of extracellular vesicles as diagnostic biomarkers, drug delivery vehicles, and cell-free therapeutics across a range of diseases, while acknowledging persistent challenges in standardizing production, purification, cargo loading, and targeted delivery. The review concludes that robust, standardized, and scalable protocols will be essential before these vesicles can be successfully translated into routine clinical use.
items.citation: Madison Schank, Juan Zhao, L Wang et al.. Extracellular Vesicles: A Comprehensive Review of Their Origins, Functions, and Therapeutic Potential. Biomedicines. 2026

items.title: Analytical Performances of Polymer-Based Biosensors for Real Samples Application
items.summary: This review examined how polymer-based biosensors perform when applied to complex real-world samples across food, beverage, environmental, and clinical contexts. The authors conducted a meta-trend analysis of nearly a hundred original research articles spanning a decade, evaluating four distinct polymer classes—conductive polymers, redox-mediator polymers, hydrogels, and molecularly imprinted polymers—across electrochemical and other detection modalities. Each polymer class was found to offer distinct advantages, with conductive polymers reducing interference at low operating potentials, hydrogels preserving enzyme function in protein-rich matrices, and molecularly imprinted polymers delivering stability for trace-level detection in harsh conditions. However, the review exposes substantial validation gaps in the published literature, with the vast majority of studies omitting limits of quantification and roughly a third lacking reproducibility or precision data, undermining confidence in reported performance. The authors identify maintaining consistent calibration across different hostile sample matrices as the central obstacle to commercial deployment, while pointing to emerging architectures such as nanocapsulation, hierarchical nanocomposites, and microneedle-integrated systems as promising routes toward improved fouling resistance and operational stability.
items.citation: Marcello Mascini, Sara Palmieri, Fabiola Eugelio et al.. Analytical Performances of Polymer-Based Biosensors for Real Samples Application. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: An integrated electrochemical platform for low-volume biosensing
items.summary: This paper developed a fully integrated electrochemical biosensing platform designed to address limitations of conventional screen-printed electrode workflows, particularly for low-volume samples. The system combines a custom three-dimensional-printed flow cell, a microfluidic pumping module, and a graphical user interface that synchronizes instrument control, data acquisition, and on-board analysis. Using double-stranded DNA as a model analyte, the platform was evaluated using chronoamperometry under continuous flow, demonstrating a linear calibration range and supporting limited electrode reuse through an electrochemical regeneration step, with signal quality declining across successive cycles. Compared to manual pipette-based delivery, the automated system achieved comparable sensitivity while improving reproducibility, reducing baseline drift, and decreasing operator hands-on time. The authors conclude that the platform provides a compact and programmable foundation for low-volume electrochemical assays with potential adaptation to point-of-care and field deployment contexts.
items.citation: Fatma Kurul, Damla Aydoğan, Dogukan Topcu et al.. An integrated electrochemical platform for low-volume biosensing. npj Biosensing. 2026

items.title: Biomaterials in personalized drug delivery: innovations, challenges, and future directions
items.summary: This review examines the role of biomaterials in drug delivery, with a focus on how advances in materials science and nanotechnology are enabling more precise, personalized therapeutic strategies. The authors survey a broad range of biomaterial classes—including polymers, ceramics, metals, and composites—describing how their tunable physicochemical properties, such as degradation kinetics and surface chemistry, can be engineered to achieve controlled drug release, protect fragile therapeutics, and improve accumulation at target tissues. Nanostructured carriers such as liposomes, micelles, and dendrimers are highlighted for their capacity to enhance solubility, cellular uptake, and site-specific targeting through size manipulation and surface functionalization. Despite substantial technological progress, the review identifies persistent barriers to clinical translation, including immune responses to biomaterials, manufacturing variability, unpredictable long-term biodegradation, and regulatory hurdles around scalable production. The authors conclude that future development must prioritize precision fabrication, manufacturing-practice compatibility, and patient-specific design to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and clinical application.
items.citation: Adna Hrapović, Nadia Islam, Asmaa Al Bourghli et al.. Biomaterials in personalized drug delivery: innovations, challenges, and future directions. PeerJ. 2026

items.title: ViTacPhys: Physical Property-Aware Grasping from Human Visual-Tactile Demonstrations
items.summary: This paper investigates how explicit object physical properties, specifically mass, friction coefficient, and stiffness, can be estimated from human visual-tactile demonstrations and used to improve robotic grasping. The authors developed ViTacPhys, a framework combining temporal visual-tactile modeling, cross-attention multimodal fusion, and vision-language model priors, trained on demonstrations collected from a diverse set of rigid and deformable objects. The system achieves high accuracy in classifying mass and friction coefficient and low error in predicting continuous stiffness, both for seen and held-out objects. To deploy the system on a robot, the authors transferred the human-trained model using limited robot teleoperation data, video augmentation, and matched human demonstrations, enabling an online adaptive grasping policy conditioned on estimated physical properties. The resulting policy achieves strong grasping success rates on both familiar and novel objects, with force profiles that more closely resemble human teleoperation than a baseline method, demonstrating the practical value of explicit physical property estimation for adaptive robotic manipulation.
items.citation: Yiwen Liu, Yujun Zhu, Kui Jia et al.. ViTacPhys: Physical Property-Aware Grasping from Human Visual-Tactile Demonstrations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Magic Velocity Selection in Atom Interferometry
items.summary: The paper investigates a systematic error source in atom interferometry arising from the use of velocity-selective Raman transitions to prepare atomic ensembles. Differential light shifts between atomic energy levels cause the selected velocity distribution to depend on laser beam intensity, creating spatial correlations between atom velocity and position within the beam. The study demonstrates that these correlated distributions interact with detuning-dependent systematic effects in a Bragg diffraction-based simultaneous conjugate Ramsey-Bordé interferometer, producing significant systematic phase shifts. The authors identify a "magic" detuning for the velocity selection process at which these spatially inhomogeneous effects cancel, suppressing the problematic phase shifts. Operating at this magic detuning is proposed as a practical strategy for eliminating a key source of systematic error in high-precision atom interferometry aimed at sub-part-per-billion accuracy.
items.citation: Yuno Iwasaki, Jack Roth, Madeline Bernstein et al.. Magic Velocity Selection in Atom Interferometry. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Truthful Calibration Measures for Sequential Prediction
items.summary: This paper investigates the theoretical foundations of calibration measures for sequential probabilistic prediction, focusing on whether desirable properties can coexist. The central question is whether exact truthfulness—meaning a forecaster cannot benefit by misreporting probabilities—can be simultaneously achieved alongside completeness and soundness, which together ensure the measure correctly identifies both good and bad calibration. The authors resolve this question negatively, proving that exact truthfulness is fundamentally incompatible with completeness and soundness even in the simple setting of independent binary outcomes. Having established this impossibility, they demonstrate that approximate truthfulness does not suffer the same fate, providing two general reductions from any base calibration measure that yield additively and multiplicatively approximately truthful variants. Applying the multiplicative reduction, they construct a family of sound and complete calibration measures with improved approximate-truthfulness guarantees, strengthening prior results in the literature.

items.title: TurboBias 2.0: Streaming Context-Biasing for Production-Efficient ASR Systems
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of context-biasing in production automatic speech recognition systems, where user-specified phrases must be accurately recognized under real-world constraints such as low latency and high throughput. The authors developed TurboBias 2.0, a framework built on Transducer-based ASR that extends a GPU-accelerated biasing approach with case-insensitive boosting graphs and per-stream batched decoding, enabling each utterance in a batch to maintain its own independent context configuration. This design allows multiple simultaneous users to benefit from personalized context lists without those lists being shared or mixed across users. The framework supports both offline and streaming inference modes and is compatible with greedy and beam-search decoding strategies. Experiments demonstrate that TurboBias 2.0 improves recognition accuracy for contextual phrases while maintaining the low latency and high throughput required for production deployment.
items.citation: Vladimir Bataev, Lilit Grigoryan, Andrei Andrusenko et al.. TurboBias 2.0: Streaming Context-Biasing for Production-Efficient ASR Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution
items.summary: This paper addresses the unreliability of using natural-language workflows as executable instructions for AI agents, identifying core problems such as implicit data dependencies and agent failures under complex or lengthy control logic. The authors propose Artic, a compiler that transforms natural-language workflows into a structured, artifact-driven representation where each step explicitly declares what information it reads and writes, with constraints on outputs and explicit control flow routing. The compiler also identifies steps that place excessive burden on agent execution and refines them through constrained optimization, while validating the transformation using decomposed faithfulness checks and scenario-based dry runs. Evaluated across a large set of problem instances drawn from real-world domain workflows, Artic substantially improves task resolution rates compared to using the original text workflows. The system also demonstrates markedly greater consistency when the compiled workflows are executed by different models or run repeatedly, suggesting the approach improves both reliability and generalizability of agent-executed procedures.
items.citation: Xiangzhe Xu, Hanxi Guo, Guangyu Shen et al.. Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Efficient Event Generation for High-Multiplicity LHC Processes: An End-to-End GPU Workflow with Normalizing Flows
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of generating large samples of unweighted events for high-multiplicity particle collision processes at the LHC, where matrix-element evaluations are expensive and unweighting efficiencies are low. The authors developed the first end-to-end GPU-resident event-generation workflow by integrating normalizing flows as phase-space proposals with the parton-level event generator Pepper, keeping all data exchanges between the machine-learning control layer and the physics generator directly in device memory to minimize overhead. Helicity-conditioned coupling flows are trained with online updates and sample replay, and both subprocess-specific and grouped conditional flow architectures are evaluated across complete proton-proton collision processes involving multiple final-state jets. Benchmarked on several high-multiplicity processes, including up to five-jet final states with electroweak bosons or top-quark pairs, the workflow was used to produce enormous unweighted event samples on a small cluster of GPUs. The approach achieves end-to-end speedups of up to two orders of magnitude compared to standalone conventional generation, reducing what would otherwise be a multi-week computation to less than a day and offering a practical path toward alleviating the Monte Carlo statistics bottleneck in collider physics.
items.citation: Enrico Bothmann, Joshua Isaacson, Claudius Krause et al.. Efficient Event Generation for High-Multiplicity LHC Processes: An End-to-End GPU Workflow with Normalizing Flows. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for rapid, decentralized testing outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors surveyed the full diagnostic workflow by organizing their analysis around three core operational steps: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. Extraction strategies reviewed include magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic approaches, with emphasis on simplicity and equipment-free operation. Amplification methods such as PCR, NASBA, RPA, and LAMP were evaluated for their adaptation to portable, low-power, and rapid conditions, while detection platforms ranged from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors exploiting CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch mechanisms. The review concludes that combining these elements can yield sensitive, selective, and economically viable nucleic acid diagnostics capable of meeting point-of-care demands for infectious disease identification.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Detection of Viral Nucleic Acid in Specimens Spotted on Commercial Filter Papers: A Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.summary: This review and meta-analysis examined the effectiveness of commercial filter paper matrices for collecting, transporting, and storing biological samples for viral nucleic acid detection across human and veterinary pathogens. The authors systematically searched major scientific databases following established guidelines, calculating nucleic acid detection rates from eligible studies and analyzing them using multilevel meta-analysis to account for clustering within studies. A large number of studies covering dozens of filter paper types were included, with cellulose-based products predominating in the literature alongside polyester and glass fiber substrates. Detection rates varied considerably both by filter paper type and by virus target, and filter paper composition along with experimental conditions such as storage temperature, drying time, and humidity were found to influence viral nucleic acid recovery. The authors conclude that recovery and detection of viral nucleic acid from filter paper is highly variable and that more rigorous, standardized experimental designs are needed to allow meaningful comparisons of filter paper performance across a range of conditions.
items.citation: Armenta-Leyva B, Munguía-Ramírez B, Kuennen B et al.. Detection of Viral Nucleic Acid in Specimens Spotted on Commercial Filter Papers: A Review and Meta-Analysis.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A, a quantitative PCR assay originally designed for throat swabs, for detecting *Streptococcus pyogenes* in pediatric pleural fluids, a context where prompt diagnosis is critical for both patient management and public health contact tracing. Researchers compared the assay against bacterial culture and a laboratory-developed PCR targeting a different gene, using a convenience sample of pleural fluid specimens that included both positive and negative cases. The Xpert assay achieved perfect agreement with the composite reference standard and the laboratory-developed PCR, detecting all positive specimens, whereas culture alone identified fewer than half of the true positives. These findings demonstrate that molecular testing substantially outperforms culture for recovering Group A streptococcus from pleural fluid, likely because many patients had already received antibiotics before sample collection. The authors conclude that the Xpert assay offers both superior sensitivity and faster turnaround time, supporting its clinical utility for diagnosing invasive Group A streptococcal disease from sterile-site specimens in children.
items.citation: Amaral G, Gadkar VJ, Almodahka A et al.. Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a multifunctional platform with broad applicability across energy, environmental, and healthcare domains. The authors comprehensively survey the synthesis chemistry and property modification strategies that underpin graphene oxide's distinctive characteristics, including its tunable band gap, high surface area, structural flexibility, and capacity for surface functionalization spanning zero- to three-dimensional nanostructural configurations. The review covers applications in environmental remediation such as adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of microplastics, pathogens, and toxic compounds, as well as energy-related uses including carbon dioxide photoreduction, hydrogen production, and battery technologies. Sensing applications, including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for ultrasensitive molecular detection and gas sensing, alongside healthcare platforms, are also assessed. The authors acknowledge that despite its transformative potential, graphene oxide faces practical challenges around scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility, and they propose possible solutions to enable its sustainable real-world and industrial deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development
items.summary: This narrative review examines the global threat posed by antimicrobial resistance, focusing on bacterial pathogens designated as priorities by the World Health Organization. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which these pathogens evade existing antibiotics, encompassing reduced membrane permeability, efflux pumps, enzymatic inactivation, target modification, biofilm formation, and horizontal gene transfer. The review critically evaluates why conventional antibiotic discovery pipelines have struggled to keep pace with resistance, and assesses a range of emerging therapeutic strategies—including artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, phage therapy, antimicrobial peptides, CRISPR-based approaches, and natural product-derived compounds—with attention to their translational challenges, toxicity, and regulatory barriers. The authors also highlight the clinical and economic burden of resistant infections and stress the importance of antimicrobial stewardship and surveillance within a One Health framework that integrates human, animal, and environmental health sectors. Overall, the review argues that overcoming the challenge of priority resistant pathogens will require coordinated, multidisciplinary efforts spanning molecular biology, pharmacology, clinical translation, and public health policy.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Mahmoud M. Dahab et al.. The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Fluorescence-Guided Chitosan and Eugenol-Based Carbon Dots for Comprehensive Infection Control and In Vitro Wound-Healing Applications in Dentistry
items.summary: Researchers developed chitosan–eugenol carbon dots as a multifunctional nanomaterial platform aimed at addressing both infection control and tissue regeneration in dental applications, with a focus on Streptococcus mutans, a key bacterium associated with dental caries and pulp inflammation. The carbon dots were synthesized from biocompatible chitosan and eugenol, then characterized for their structural and elemental properties using electron microscopy and energy dispersive X-ray analysis, revealing spherical nanoparticles with successful incorporation of carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen heteroatoms. Antibacterial performance was evaluated through minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentration assays, demonstrating concentration-dependent inhibition of the target pathogen. Biocompatibility was assessed using fibroblast viability, morphology, and migration assays, all of which confirmed that the material supported cell health and promoted cell movement indicative of wound-healing potential. The authors conclude that combining chitosan and eugenol within a carbon dot framework yields a synergistic nanoplatform with fluorescence properties, strong antibacterial activity, and favorable cytocompatibility, positioning it as a promising candidate for treating oral infections and supporting tissue repair in dentistry.
items.citation: N. Narayanan, Aruchamy Mohanprasanth, Natesan Thirumalaivasan. Fluorescence-Guided Chitosan and Eugenol-Based Carbon Dots for Comprehensive Infection Control and In Vitro Wound-Healing Applications in Dentistry. Dentistry Journal. 2026
